title: FOCUS - Zloty soars as crawl cut hopes emerge.
text:
WARSAW, May 5 (Reuters) - A member of Poland's monetary council re-ignited hopes of a near-term reduction of the zloty's gradual or crawling devaluation, sending the zloty to a new all-time high on Tuesday. 

 Monetary Policy Council (RPP) member Marek Dabrowski said the central bank's main policy goal of pulling inflation down to the 9.5 percent envisaged in the budget this year was not possible unless the zloty's devaluation factor was reduced further. 

 The 10-member RPP cut the zloty's crawl to 0.8 percent per month against a basket of five Western currencies from 1.0 percent in late February, and most analysts did not expect any further significant reductions in the crawl this year. 

 Dabrowski said monthly inflation had to average about 0.4 percent for the rest of 1998 if Poland was to meet its CPI target, which was equal to half of the zloty's monthly crawl. 

 Analysts said even though Dabrowski's views were probably not shared by many of his less outspoken RPP colleagues, his arguments, published in the heavyweight Rzeczpospolita daily, had brought an important issue out into the open. 

 "Monetary authorities stand before an important dilemma: either adjust the exchange rate mechanism so that it enables effective anti-inflationary policy, or revise money supply upward and interest rates downwards," Dabrowski wrote. 

 Analysts said any reduction in the crawling peg would have to be accompanied by a cut in official interest rates to keep foreign capital from flooding Poland's fixed income market and potentially destabilising the economy. 

 "If the crawl is cut then interest rates must follow," said Krzysztof Rybinski, chief analyst at ING Barings in Warsaw. 

 But Rybinski added that interest rates would still remain high in real terms to keep the economy from over-heating and again building up inflationary pressure. 

 Analysts said the RPP would rather meet the inflation target than keep a stable currency, which could translate into a crawl cut sometime in the third quarter of 1998. 

 "My forecast is for the rate of crawl to be cut around September from 0.8 to 0.6 (percent per month) but if there is pressure on the currency and the central bank widens the band then the reduction could happen earlier," said Beshada Madi, vice president at Morgan Stanley in London. 

 Analysts said that after inflation fell more than five points to 13.2 percent in 1997, slower price growth had to be maintained to keep inflation expectations on the decline. 

 "It is important to see CPI growth continue to go down, so the economy doesn't stabilise at a high inflation level, making further reductions more difficult," said Jesper Dannesboe, economist at ABN-AMRO in London. 

 On Tuesday the zloty hit a record high of 8.31 percent above its targeted basket level - the mid-point of its 20 percent trading band - despite an estimated $100 million dollar-buying intervention by the central bank. 

 The zloty topped eight percent above parity for the first time on Monday, ending the day fixed at 8.03 percent. 

 Analysts said the zloty could again be pushed into battle with central bank interventions as early as Wednesday, when Poland holds a 1.1 billion zloty auction of popular two-and five-year fixed rate T-bonds. 

 "We can expect large demand especially for five-year papers tomorrow as people find Poland's real interest rates extremely attractive," said Ryszard Bublik, fixed income dealer at Nomura International in London. title: Polish RPP hopes rate cut to slow zloty's rise.
text:
WARSAW, April 22 (Reuters) - Poland's Monetary Policy Council (RPP) hopes its Wednesday cut in the main money market rate will ease upward pressure on the zloty and limit the need for central bank forex market interventions, a member of RPP said. 

 The RPP cut its money market intervention rate by one point to 23 percent on Wednesday, while leaving Poland's main interest rates unchanged at 27 percent and 24.5 percent. 

 "Obviously, a cut in interest rates will, as usual, cause the currency to weaken...this is the direction of our activities, in view of what is happening in the market," Grzegorz Wojtowicz told Reuters after the council's meeting on Wednesday. 

 Asked if the central bank would have to continue to stage forex market interventions to keep the zloty from rising, Wojtowicz said, "I hope for more peace after this rate cut." 

 Large foreign inflows into Polish high-yielding treasuries have pushed the zloty up by more than six percentage points since the start of the year and sparked repeated central bank dollar-and mark-buying interventions. 

 Wojtowicz said he hoped that if Poland's economic situation developed well, the Wednesday decision to cut the intervention rate could be the starting point of a longer process of declining interest rates. 

 "I hope so," he said, referring to a hoped-for beginning of some longer process of interest-rate declines. "It's hard to imagine a country having such high real interest rates."

title: Poland's reforms set stage for lower rates - finmin.
text:
NEW YORK, April 20 (Reuters) - Poland's Finance Minister Leszek Balcerowicz said on Monday policies to reduce the budget deficit would set the stage for lower interest rates, but declined comment on whether the Polish central bank should cut rates at this week's policy meeting. 

 "I am trying to create a scope, by reducing the budget deficit, for at some stage some response for the lowering of interest rates," Balcerowicz told Reuters Television here. 

 The government's efforts to reduce public spending and accelerate privatization were critical to dealing with heavy foreign capital inflows coming into Poland, he said. 

 But the finance minister said he did not want to influence the monetary policy of Poland's independent central bank. 

 "The monetary council of the central bank will meet the day after tomorrow, I wouldn't like to preempt their decision," Balcerowicz said. 

 Poland's central bank chief Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz reiterated over the weekend that a cut in interest rates was possible this year if the economy developed well. 

 The Polish zloty soared to record highs on Monday amid strong foreign interest in Polish treasury paper, forcing the currency to close at 7.89/7.85 percent above the trading band center, against Friday's 7.60/7.57 percent. 

 The National Bank of Poland did not intervene to slow the zloty's rise on Monday. Last week it spent an estimated $130 million. 

 Warsaw analysts said the central bank's Monetary Policy Council may have to take decisions to cool the market's strong pro-zloty sentiment, even though the the Council was not expected to lower rates until the third quarter. 

 Some analysts suggested the central bank would widen the zloty's 20-percent trading band or could stop announcing the daily parity rate to create more uncertainty for speculators.

title: Emerging market  forex  - Asia under a cloud again.
text:
LONDON, April 16 (Reuters) - Fresh slippage in emerging Asian currencies was the focus of Thursday's trading session, standing in contrast to continued strength in U.S. stocks and persistent bullishness in emerging Europe. 

 Renewed weakness in the Japanese yen and a second-quarter reappraisal of regional stock markets by foreign investors has conspired to push emerging Asian currencies lower too, analysts said. 

 The Malaysian ringgit underperformed on Thursday, weighed down by a slide in the local bourse of almost seven percent since last week amid rising concerns about corporate failures and a steep economic slowdown. 

 "Asian equities are going to see a reversal of first-quarter rallies as we start to see the economic pain of the last year's financial shock in the form of bankruptcies, liquidations and unemployment," said Paul MacNamara, emerging markets economist at Julius Baer Investments. 

 "Renewed equity weakness is almost certainly going to feed through to the currency markets as well." 

 The failure of this week's meeting of the Group of Seven industrialised nations (G7) to address any concrete proposals for boosting Japan's moribund economy also sent the yen sliding through 130 per dollar overnight and helped boost the dollar across Asia. 

 "People made a lot of money buying Asian currency baskets in the first quarter of the year and they are basically reluctant to push their luck," said one trader at a U.S. investment bank in London. 

 In emerging Europe, the zloty continued to defy the National Bank of Poland and pushed higher again on Thursday despite Wednesday's intervention to cap it. 

 Benign March inflation date boosted the Treasury bill market as well and a perception the central bank is intent on squeezing inflation even further has dampened any speculation of a cut in attractive official interest rates. 

 "The central bank wants interest rates to remain high, the currency weaker and more uncertainty in day-to-day dealings. These are conflicting policy aims," said MacNamara at Julius Baer. 

 "The problem is the market still sees this as a one-way bet and intervention only provides better forex levels to buy." 

 Elsewhere, the Russian rouble was steady as Friday's second Duma vote on Sergei Kiriyenko's nomination as Prime Minister was awaited. 

 Kiriyenko was rejected by the Duma last week but President Boris Yeltsin said he will dissolve the lower house if his candidate is rejected three times. 

 The Kremlin denied speculation on Thursday that Yeltsin had second thoughts about his choice of the 35-year old Kiriyenko as premier. 

 Analysts said that while the market still remained relatively sanguine about the political hiatus in Moscow, fresh concerns about weakness in world oil prices were probably more of a concern. 

 Statistics out on Thursday showed Russian gross domestic product growth was flat year-on-year in the first quarter of this year, down from a rise of 0.8 percent in the last quarter of 1997. 

 Oil export revenues in Russia are crucial to its budgetary targets this year. Prices firmed on Wednesday and Thursday recovering losses earlier in the week as Venezuelan officials reiterated their commitment to production cuts. 

 The Venezuelan bolivar slipped sharply late Wednesday and has been depreciating in April at a faster rate than in previous months.

title: Emerging market  forex  - Zloty rise tests NBP again.
text:
LONDON, April 15 (Reuters) - A renewed rally in the zloty drew fresh bouts of intervention from the National Bank of Poland (NBP) on Wednesday but many analysts remain bullish on both the currency and local debt instruments. 

 Signs of moderating Polish inflation and central bank determination to squeeze the inflation rate further are combining to keep upward pressure on the zloty and both short-and long-term zloty debt, dealers said. 

 This is partly why the latest round of central bank zloty sales, which were conducted on Wednesday at between 7.30 and 7.50 per cent above the zloty's parity against a target basket of currencies, had only a minor impact. 

 The zloty was fixed after the intervention at 7.27 percent above parity. 

 The latest zloty surge started yesterday after NBP president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz was quoted in a newspaper as saying the currency should strengthen in the long term to help curb inflation to 9.5 percent this year - a target she said was still possible. 

 "These comments reinforce the market view that given a choice between continued zloty strength or lower interest rates, the central bank will opt for the former," said one dealer at a French bank in London. 

 "Unless the market appetite for high yields shifts suddenly, then further zloty upside is still possible despite the intervention." 

 The central bank currently has a 10 percent daily fluctuation limit either side of its target parity. 

 The Polish Central Statistical Office said on Wednesday that annual Polish inflation fell to 13.9 percent in March from 14.2 percent in February. 

 In its latest emerging markets research note, investment bank Salomon Smith Barney said it recommended overweight positions toward Polish short and long term local currency instruments and external sovereign bonds. 

 "Some further upside on the zloty remains in the period ahead as the authorities cope with the surge in capital flows," the report said. 

 However, JP Morgan's latest Global Markets Outlook research note warned that investors' thirst for high yields in Europe may be satisfied for now and it recommended reducing exposure to the zloty market along with a cut in sterling holdings. 

 Buoyant international markets, led by the relentless rise in U.S. stocks, underpinned most other emerging markets on Wednesday. 

 The Czech crown shrugged off a health scare for President Vaclav Havel, who was said to have recovered well from emergency surgery. 

 The rouble nudged lower ahead of Friday's latest Duma vote on the new Russian prime minister. 

 The Israeli shekel recovered part of Tuesday's sharp drop but further volatility is expected ahead of foreign exchange market liberalisation next month. 

 Persistent concerns about the Japanese economy and the yen continued to weigh on emerging Asia units, as many investors were tempted to take profits on strong first quarter gains. 

 The Indonesian rupiah underperformed in the region on Wednesday. 

 The strong Dow Jones performance also lifted Latin American currencies, with the International Monetary Fund's maintenance of its 4.8 percent Mexican growth forecast for 1998 helping the peso.

title: Zloty softens but upward sentiment intact.
text:
WARSAW, March 31 (Reuters) - The zloty softened in dull trade on Tuesday, but dealers said the unit could soon test the psychological barrier at seven percent above the trading band centre if foreign flows into Polish treasuries increased. 

 "The zloty market was quite balanced on Tuesday, but expectations are that the zloty will continue to test its upside in the near term despite a threat of a central bank intervention," said Wojciech Trzepizur, forex dealer at BRE SA. 

 The National Bank of Poland (NBP) staged no forex market interventions on Tuesday after buying an estimated $55 million on Monday when the zloty was at between 6.85 and 6.7 percent above the trading band centre. 

 "The resistance level set by the NBP will continue to be tested and if the central bank is quiet for several days then the zloty will rise again," BRE's Trzepizur said. 

 The zloty closed on Tuesday at 6.78/6.74 percent stronger than the parity rate against Monday's 6.81/6.79 percent. 

 It ended at 3.4465/85 to the dollar against 3.4315/25 on Monday and at 1.8671/76 to the mark against 1.8720/25. 

 Analysts said large foreign interest at Wednesday's primary fixed rate note auctions could add momentum to the zloty's rise later this week. 

 "If there was huge demand (at Wednesday's tenders) the zloty could get a boost, but I would suspect the central bank would come in again and prevent any more gains," said Ryszard Bublik, dealer at Nomura International in London. 

 On Wednesday the finance ministry offers one billion zlotys of two-and five-year T-bonds as well as 450 million zlotys of fixed rate notes, maturing on October 12, 2002. 

 Analysts expected the average yield of five-year T-bonds to inch up to around 19.0 percent from 18.7 percent at the auction in early March. The average yield of two-year notes was seen at 22.50 on Wednesday against 21.5 at the previous auction. 

 "Compared to the previous tender, yields should go slightly higher. Foreign demand at the auctions will probably be large, but I don't think investors will bid aggressively," said Marcin Rzechowski, fixed income dealer at Societe Generale in Warsaw. 

 The average yield of four-year notes was expected to inch up to about 19.8 percent against 19.4 percent at a similar auction on March 4. 

 On the money market short-term rates inched down on the first day of the new monthly reserve period. Overnight rates closed at 23.90/24.25 against opening 24.40/24.75 percent.

title: Emerging market  forex  - Central Europe stays bid.
text:
LONDON, March 30 (Reuters) - Central European currencies picked up where they left off last week, with the Czech crown pushing seven-month highs on Monday and continued demand for zlotys drawing fresh intervention from Poland's central bank. 

 Elsewhere, the Ukrainian hryvnia was little moved by early indications that Sunday's parliamentary elections showed the Communist Party was likely to win most votes. 

 Meantime emerging Asian currencies were mixed to a touch softer, with analysts expecting a period of consolidation there after recent strong gains. 

 "Central Europe is outperforming again and this week's EU accession talks serve as a reminder about why there's a particular edge to that story, " said a trader at a U.S. bank. "Everywhere else, there seems to be a bit of levelling-off." 

 Talks on European Union membership for Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovenia, Estonia and Cyprus start on Tuesday. 

 The mark/Czech crown rate broke below 18.40 on Monday for the first time since last August. 

 The crown has been boosted in an environment of calm international markets as investors search for high yields despite underlying political uncertainty ahead of June's elections. 

 Dealers said the next key chart support was the lows from last August about 18.26. If the mark was to breach this support, it would then return to levels not seen since just prior to last May's Czech devaluation. 

 The National Bank of Poland intervened on several occasions on Monday to sell zlotys for dollars. Regular bouts of intervention last week to cap the zloty have failed to depress the unit. 

 The zloty was trading about midsession at about 6.83 percent above its parity against a basket of officially-targeted currencies, close to where it was prior to the first round of central bank sales on Monday. 

 Dealers said the 7.0 percent barrier looks to be a sensitive level for the central bank. 

 "The only thing the NBP can realistically do here is to slow the upside," said one analyst at a European central bank. 

 "It can't really hope to depress the zloty for long because the positive fundamentals driving it higher are likely to remain in place for at least another six-to-twelve months." 

 Investors bid for 1.8 billion zlotys of Treasury bills at a 900 million zloty auction on Monday. 

 In Asia earlier, the Indonesian rupiah edged lower amid some profit-taking on its recent rally. 

 But analysts said sentiment toward the currency remained positive as the outcome of talks between the government and the International Monetary Fund on the country's debt restructuring are awaited. 

 Some analysts said a deal was possible as soon as Wednesday.

title: Emerging market  forex  - crown rallies, zloty capped.
text:
LONDON, March 25 (Reuters) - Demand for central European currencies remained robust on Wednesday, but the Czech crown and Polish zloty diverged amid conflicting signals from their central banks. 

 The National Bank of Poland (NBP) intervened for the second consecutive day to sell zlotys for dollars after the zloty had quickly bounced back in the wake of Tuesday's intervention. 

 The Czech crown strengthened, meantime, after vice-governor of the Czech central bank Jan Vit said the bank was not considering easing monetary policy any time soon as it was battling to meet its inflation targets. 

 "The central bank comments caused the latest move in the crown but I'd be worried about mark/Czech about these levels," said Nick Douch, corporate risk adviser at Barclays Capital. 

 "Quite apart from the disappointing inflation picture, the outcome of the June elections is looking more and more uncertain and further crown strength runs the risk of re-igniting current account problems." 

 Poland, on the other hand, remains attractive despite the central bank's protests, and the magnet of 20-percent-plus yields is likely to keep investors coming back, Douch said. 

 Despite reports of dissent within the NBP over Tuesday's intervention, estimated at about $35 million, the central bank sold zlotys on several occasions again on Wednesday. 

 The sales started as the zloty traded near 6.75 percent above parity against an officially-targeted basket of currencies - the same level where it began intervening on Tuesday. 

 The zloty edged back below 6.50 percent in response to the latest wave of central bank sales, from 6.78/54 at the open. 

 "The seven percent area, which was the limit of the old band, is obviously a sensitive area for the central bank but they would want to be careful about drawing lines in the sand,' said one dealer at a European bank. 

 "The bulk of the foreign investment in this market is in for the interest-rate carry, not the currency appreciation, and the zloty would have to be at a risk of a move back below parity before that sort of investment is deterred." 

 Mark/Czech, meantime, slid to test 18.50 from just above 18.60 late Tuesday as Vit's comments reinforced technical signals. Trendline resistance just above 18.64 is reinforcing the strength of the crown, dealers said. 

 Elsewhere in emerging Europe, the Romanian leu firmed after the central bank sold dollars for the second time this week. 

 The leu had skidded to about 8,500 per dollar from 8,050 late last week as local dealers cited foreign selling of fixed income investments. 

 "The central bank has a strong grip on this market, mainly because there's very little foreign money in there," said Douch at Barclays. "But investors are fed up with the slowdown in the whole reform process and temptation is to pull out unless there is some movement." 

 Senior Romanian officials on Monday said the country will notify the International Monetary Fund that it accepts Article Eight of the IMF treaty relating to current account convertibility of the leu. 

 Turkish markets' strong performance continued on Wednesday. 

 Easing tensions between the government and the army in Turkey have boosted fixed income markets as concern about a snap election recedes and investors focus on high nominal yields and expectations of slowing inflation. 

 Turkish bond yields dropped 160 basis points on Wednesday, bring the fall since Friday to about 500 bp. The Turkish central bank also sold lira for dollars in two rounds on Wednesday. 

 In Asia earlier, the Malaysian ringgit and the Indonesian rupiah strengthened. 

 The ringgit was lifted as Bank Negara's latest report stressed the need to keep monetary policy tight. The rupiah was boosted amid speculation a new IMF package is imminent and amid optimism about the country's debt restructuring.

title: Polish c.bank Tue action stirs monetary council.
text:
WARSAW, March 25 (Reuters) - The National Bank of Poland's Tuesday interventions against the zloty caused a stir in the monetary policy council (RPP) as some of its members said the RPP had agreed with the bank's board to leave the zloty alone. 

 "I do not understand why the NBP intervened since we agreed that it would not do it," the Gazeta Wyborcza daily reported an anonymous council member as saying. 

 "Maybe the situation was extraordinary, but the bank's chiefs will have to explain this," the daily quoted the RPP member as saying. 

 The monetary policy council is a 10-person body, headed by the central bank president, which sets the NBP's monetary policy alone and directs its foreign exchange policy in cooperation with the finance and economy ministries. 

 On Tuesday the NBP bought an estimated $35 million on the interbank market when the zloty was at between 6.7-6.2 percent stronger than parity. 

 But another RPP member Cezary Jozefiak told Reuters he would not require any explanations from the NBP board, which implements the monetary council's decisions. 

 "The agreement between the RPP and the NBP board was that the NBP should act in such a way so as not to make the interpretation of the actions easy," Jozefiak said. 

 "I don't know what the whole council will want, but to me the board does not have to explain anything," he said. 

 The Tuesday interventions came after the central bank president told the PAP news agency the bank would intervene when the zloty approached to the end of its 10-percent daily trading band on either side of the parity rate.

title: Zloty eyes profit-taking dip after c. bank action.
text:
WARSAW, March 24 (Reuters) - Poland's forex market will stay jittery on Wednesday and some players may book profits on the zloty's recent gains after the central bank unexpectedly bought dollars on the market on Tuesday, analysts said. 

 The National Bank of Poland (NBP) intervened for the first time in over a month, buying an estimated $35 million when the zloty was between 6.7-6.2 percent above the parity rate. 

 The zloty closed on Tuesday at 6.26/6.22 percent above the parity rate against Monday's 6.76/6.70 percent close. 

 It closed at 3.4420/40 to the dollar against 3.4260/80 on Monday and at 1.8843/48 to the mark against 1.8737/50. 

 "It seems that investors received a clear signal that it's time to take profits. If players start closing positions we can see a major weakening of the zloty," said Zbigniew Chmielewski, treasurer at ING Barings in Warsaw. 

 "Without the NBP's help, the zloty may even slide to around 5.0 percent from parity," Chmielewski added. 

 But other analysts said the zloty could find support much earlier. 

 "The market is looking at six percent as a pretty strong support level, so profit taking seems limited," said Matthew Vogel, economist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette. 

 Analysts said Poland's strong fundamentals and lucrative yields on longer-term treasuries should help the zloty rebound from any dip. 

 "We could see some profit-taking, but it's going to be only temporarily. If nothing else negative happens, we will see investors coming in again," said Zsolt Papp, emerging markets economist at UBS in London. 

 Dealers said Poland's secondary treasury market stayed calm on Tuesday. If the zloty weakened, fresh capital could flow into attractive fixed rate notes, they added. 

 "The central bank wants to pull the zloty down to 6.0 percent, but the weaker the currency is, the bigger foreign interest in our T-bonds becomes," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, senior fixed income dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

title: Emerging market  forex  - zloty falls as NBP sells.
text:
LONDON, March 24 (Reuters) - The recent rally in emerging market currencies was interrupted on Tuesday by National Bank of Poland (NBP) intervention to cap the zloty and some disappointment at Malaysia's latest economic package. 

 While sentiment toward high-yield local currency markets in general remained robust, the NBP action and the temptation to take profits from recent sharp gains in emerging Asian units may mark a period of consolidation around the globe, dealers said. 

 The Indonesian rupiah and Philippine peso outperformed on the day in Asia, meantime, while the rouble continued to hold firm in the wake of Monday's dismissal of the Russian cabinet. 

 The zloty's retreat was the focus in European hours after the NBP sold zlotys for dollars on several occasions. 

 The currency retreated to 6.24 percent above its parity against a basket of officially-targeted currencies versus 6.78/54 percent above at the opening on Tuesday. 

 Tuesday's intervention followed the central bank's surprise decision on Monday to fix the currency at 6.51 percent above parity, well below prevailing market levels about 6.70 percent. 

 "There's been confusion over the zloty's direction over the past week, but the lower fixing on Monday and the intervention today means the central bank is saying enough is enough," said Miranda Xafa, currency strategist at Salomon Smith Barney. 

 "Fighting inflation in Poland is clearly an important policy objective but opposition to excessive currency strength shows there is also some worries about the external accounts." 

 The past week has been a roller-coaster for the zloty. 

 The volatility started with a sudden bout of profit taking last Wednesday after investment firm Goldman Sachs recommended it was time to cut long positions. 

 The zloty recovered its losses by Friday, however, and then soared to as high as 7.50 percent after reported comments, later denied, that the central bank was happy with recent strength. 

 "The sheer volatility of the zloty over the past week will probably be enough to take the pure currency speculation out of the market, but the yield story is still attractive unless you think there is going to be a complete collapse," said a trader at a U.S. investment firm. 

 The Russian rouble held firm following President Boris Yeltsin's decision to dismiss Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and his cabinet on Monday. 

 Analysts said the underlying uncertainty of Russian politics had been highlighted again, but it looked as if a reconstituted cabinet would lean toward reformers rather than signal any great change in economic policy. 

 Elsewhere in Europe, the Czech crown was steady about 18.61 per mark, with chart analysts saying there was strong trendline resistance on any uptick above 18.64. 

 In more exotic European markets, the collapse of the Belarussian rouble stole the show. 

 Local dealers said the Belarussian unit plummeted on the interbank market to as low as 64,000-69,000 per dollar against 52,000-54,000 per dollar late last week. 

 In Moscow, the Russian central bank recommended that Russian citizens refrain from trading the Belarussian unit and said it ceased quoting an official rate against the Russian rouble. 

 This was in response to the Belarussian central bank's decision on Monday to stop foreigners trading its currency. 

 The Belarussian rouble was at 45,000-47,000 to the dollar at the beginning of this year. 

 In Asia, the Malaysian ringgit erased much of Monday's gains amid profit-taking and some disappointment that a package of new economic measures announced by Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim fell short of easing restrictions on foreign investment.

text:
WARSAW, March 24 (Reuters) - Poland's central bank (NBP) on Tuesday intervened on the local forex market for the first time in a month to cool the zloty in what analysts said was a risky game which might lure short-term speculators. 

 Analysts said the NBP had to slow the zloty's rise to keep the local currency from climbing towards the top of its trading band - a situation which would lower the exchange rate risk and potentially spark more inflows into Poland. 

 "If the zloty sticks to the top of its band for long enough it starts to look like a fixed exchange rate currency of high stability - like in Hungary - encouraging even more inflows," said David Mars, economist at SCB Warburg in London. 

 On Tuesday the NBP bought roughly $35 million and pushed the zloty down to 6.26/6.22 percent on the stronger side of the trading band centre from Monday's 6.76/6.70 percent close. 

 The zloty can trade within a 10 percent band around the parity rate. It peaked at an all-time high around 7.50 percent above parity on Friday. 

 Over the last month, foreign purchases of Poland's high-yielding treasuries have pushed up the zloty more than four points against its basket without sparking any central bank actions. 

 "Interest rates right now are very high and pushing the currency weaker is going to have a potential rebound effect by bringing in more money," said Matthew Vogel, economist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette. 

 The central bank may be intervening to trigger a wave of profit-taking by currency speculators who have opened long zloty positions over the last weeks, but analysts said that this policy might not be sustainable in the longer-term. 

 "They (the NBP) are trying to weaken the zloty at a small cost...but when the currency loses strength foreigners will again enter Polish T-bonds," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, senior dealer at Bank Handlowy SA. 

 Some analysts said, however, that the Polish zloty may weaken slightly over the next several days before rebounding again amid renewed foreign interest. 

 "Players will probably wait two or three days to see what's going on and then we could see the zloty again close to about seven percent," said Zsolt Papp, economist at UBS in London. 

 Analysts said Tuesday's dollar-buying interventions were not aimed at weakening the zloty to keep the current account from deteriorating further or at setting a sure-fire resistance level for the unit. 

 "Today's interventions have very little to do with the current account gap and targeting any nominal or real exchange rate levels and everything to do with the central bank trying to retain its exchange rate flexibility and not being boxed into a corner," SCB Warburg's Mars added. 

 Some analysts said the central bank might have intervened on Tuesday after it come under fire for fixing the zloty below market close on Friday and Monday - a move some market participants branded a hidden intervention. 

Central bank officials have said past fixings were weaker than market close because the Polish zloty gained mainly on speculation and not actual capital inflows.

title: Sensitive zloty seen jittering on speculation.
text:
WARSAW, March 20 (Reuters) - Market speculation, which pushed the Polish zloty into wild swings this week, is likely to continue in the near term as players start to take profits on the unit's recent gains, analysts said on Friday. 

 The zloty rocketed more than one percentage point on Friday after the central bank chief told PAP news agency that she saw no weakening of the local currency in the short term. 

 Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said in an interview that the National Bank of Poland would intervene if the zloty approached the 10 percent level above the parity rate, remarks misinterpreted by the market as a go-ahead for a further zloty rise. 

 "Everybody knows where the upper limit of the band is, but as the market has been oversensitive, the words of the central bank's head have had an incredible impact on the market," said Krzysztof Rybinski, chief analyst at ING Barings in Warsaw. 

 Analysts said the zloty's sharp rise this week may prompt mass profit-taking and the market should find an equilibrium around six percent from the trading band centre next week. 

 "We can see the zloty moving back to six percent rather than staying at these levels where it is at the moment," said Ryszard Bublik, dealer at Nomura International in London. 

 Earlier this week, the zloty fell nearly one percentage point after U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs said investors should take profits on Poland's currency and debt instruments. 

 "This Wednesday sent shivers throughout the market as any negative signal sparks incredible foreign currency buying," said Zbigniew Chmielewski, treasurer at ING Barings in Warsaw. 

 "The market has been very sensitive since the zloty reached such dangerous levels," Chmielewski said. 

 The zloty set a new all-time high on Friday, ending the day at 7.26/6.99 percent from the trading band centre against last week's close of 5.86/5.65 percent. 

 The RPP decided on Wednesday to leave official interest rates unchanged. It also left the benchmark 28-day open market rate at the minimum level of 24 percent. 

 Dealers said the strong zloty should keep most foreigners away from Monday's one billion zloty primary T-bill auction, where yields are seen rising from the previous tender levels. 

 "If the zloty stays as strong as it is we won't see many foreign investors on Monday," said Wlodzimierz Kado, fixed income dealer at Bank Handlowy SA. 

 "Yields should move higher as these papers are not very attractive if the money market remains cash-dry," Kado said. 

 Short-term rates traded on Friday above the central bank's minimum drainage rate of 24 percent as Polish banks continued to see cash shortages on their monthly accounts. 

 Dealers expected T-bill yields to inch up to secondary market levels at Monday's tender. The benchmark 52-week paper is expected to rise to about 22.80 percent from Monday's 22.30. 

 "The 13-week bill yield should also go up by about 10 to 20 basis points at the tender," Handlowy's Kado said.

title: Polish c.bank keeps interest rates, reserves flat.
text:
WARSAW, March 18 (Reuters) - The Monetary Policy Council decided to keep the National Bank of Poland's official interest rates, the 28-day intervention rate as well as the level of banks' obligatory reserves unchanged, it said on Wednesday. 

 "The monetary policy council at its meeting on March 18... decided that the National Bank of Poland's main interest rates will stay unchanged, the 28-day intervention rate will also stay unchanged and so will the levels of banks' obligatory reserves," the council said in a statement. 

 The NBP's main rates are now at 27 and 24.5 percent and the 28-day open market operations minimum rate is 24 percent. 

 Obligatory reserves on zloty call deposits are currently at 20 percent, 11 percent on zloty term deposits and at five percent for all foreign currency deposits. 

 The Monetary Policy Council also decided to tighten control over the way banks' calculate their obligatory reserve levels every month. 

 "The basis for calculating the obligatory reserve should be the arithmetical average of the funds on accounts from all working days of the previous month," the statement said. 

 Currently the reserves are counted on the basis of an average from only three days of the previous month - the 10th, 20th and 30th day. 

 "This is meant to make the obligatory reserves a more efficient instrument," central bank president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz told a news conference.

title: EMERGING MARKETS-Zloty dliemma - shades of ERM past.
text:
LONDON, March 13 (Reuters) - The policy dilemma surrounding the surge of Poland's zloty this year has cast analysts' minds back to the monetary conundrum faced by Spain and Portugal in the early 1990s. 

 Back then, those countries were dogged by a phenomenon known by market players as "excess credibility". 

 This was where a tidal wave of foreign capital swamped the domestic market and threatened to distort domestic monetary policy by undermining the fight against inflation. 

 If the analogy proves even partly correct, some analysts argue Polish markets could be in for a rocky ride when the current euphoria over its domestic markets ebbs. 

 "We're seeing policy problems build up here, which are very similar to the 'excess credibility' story surrounding the high-yielders in the ERM in the early 1990s," said Avinash Persaud, head of currency research at JP Morgan. 

 "The Polish authorities will need to be very careful how they handle this, and investors will do well to be aware of the longer-term risks to a market in this position." 

 The zloty has risen to its highest level against the German mark in seven months and its highest against the dollar in four months. 

 More importantly, it is approaching the upper end of its permitted fluctuation range against a basket of target currencies, and the central bank will soon be obliged to cap it via direct intervention or lower interest rates. 

 Here lies the problem. Poland's inflation rate, at 13.2 percent year-on-year in January, is almost 12 percentage points higher than the European Union average. 

 As a result, it needs at least some nominal currency depreciation to maintain export competitiveness and avoid a balance of payments problem, and to get inflation down it needs to keep high interest rates. 

 With economic growth expected to remain brisk at 5.8 percent in 1998, the current account deficit is expected to widen to almost six percent of gross domestic product from 3.2 percent last year. 

 The situation is familiar. Emerging market players will look to last year's Czech crown devaluation as a model but more conventional investors may see more similarity with the European Union's recent history. 

 Spain's attempts to minimise currency volatility via membership of the EU's exchange rate mechanism sent foreign investors scrambling for the high interest rates available on peseta securities in the early 1990s. 

 These flows put downward pressure on local interest rates and distorted domestic monetary policy which is aimed a cutting high inflation rates. Central bank intervention to sell pesetas simply pumped the local market full of pesetas and pushed interest rates lower prematurely. 

 The Spanish central bank's reluctance to cut official interest rates in the face of persistently high inflation and strong domestic growth, meant the peseta was pinned for years to the upper limits of its permitted ERM bands. 

 This ultimately lead to a prolonged overvaluation of the peseta, exaggerated Spain's current account deficit and increased its dependence on foreign capital, much of which had been short-term. 

 The problem culminated in a series of peseta devaluations, following the ERM crisis of 1992. 

 "Poland is ultimately caught with conflicting inflation and exchange rate targets," said Zsolt Papp, emerging market economist at UBS. 

 "My hunch is they should concentrate on getting inflation below 10 percent and let the currency float if necessary," he said. 

 The country's expected membership of the EU within the next five or six years reinforces the attraction of locking into short-term yield of more than 20 percent. 

 Moreover, capital exchange controls on zloty trading and a officially-targeted and pre-announced monthly depreciation target for the currency, minimises currency risk in a similar way to the ERM. 

 Full liberalisation of foreign exchange markets and a removal of the crawling peg may be the only solution. 

 "Poland is ready to adopt more flexible rules as far as capital account convertibility is concerned," Stanislaw Gomulka, an economist at the London School of Economics and an independent adviser to Poland's central bank governor, said this week. 

 "But the key defence is elsewhere - the right macroeconomic 

  policy in general. In particular a low budget deficit...and also 

  structural changes," he said.

title: Polish Zloty -2: Some Expect Profit-Taking
text:
The dollar in after-hours trading is at 3.4765 zlotys (PLN), down from Tuesday afternoon's central bank fixing of PLN3.4815 and from Monday's fixing of PLN3.4895. 

 Market participants said foreign purchases of government bonds are helping to support the zloty. 

 The Deutsche mark is at PLN1.8896, down from the afternoon fixing of PLN1.9020 and from Monday afternoon's fixing of PLN1.9095. 

 Ladko said the zloty's upper limit would most likely be established by the National Bank of Poland, which, he said, may be forced to intervene to keep the zloty within its 20-point band around the parity rate. 

 The zloty could eventually be weakened by a cut in key interest rates, Ladko added. But he said high demand for credit will keep the central bank from cutting rates before summer. Other participants agreed. 

 Before the central bank widened the trading band to 20 points from 14 points two weeks ago, it intervened regularly to keep the zloty from straying by much more than 2% from parity in the strong end of the band. 

 Dealers said they were uncertain whether a new intervention level would be established within the wider band. But many said it is unlikely, since the central bank wants to encourage greater volatility in the foreign exchange market. 

 Jaroslaw Krol, chief dealer at ABN Amro Bank in Warsaw, said the zloty will next attack the level of 5.5% above the midpoint and then move to 6%. 'Only the central bank can limit the zloty,' he said. 

 Some dealers said the market will be ripe for a bout of profit-taking if the zloty gains much more. Andrzej Fiderkiewicz, a dealer at Societe Generale, said he expects the zloty to settle in a range of between 5% and 5.2% above the midpoint.

title: Foreign-charged zloty seen setting new highs.
text:
WARSAW, March 10 (Reuters) - The zloty set a new all-time high on Tuesday and dealers said continuing foreign interest in Polish longer-term fixed income instruments would keep the unit on a steady rise in the near-term. 

 "Foreign demand for Polish debt instruments has slowed to a certain extent, but strong interest in longer-term bonds is still there, so I see no reason why the zloty should weaken," said Ryszard Bublik, dealer at Nomura International in London. 

 The zloty ended on Tuesday at 5.17/5.11 percent from the parity rate against Monday's close of 4.84/4.79 percent. 

 It closed at 3.4800/25 to the dollar against 3.4900/20 on Monday and at 1.9020/30 to the mark against 1.9086/94. 

 Dealers expected the zloty to drift slowly towards 5.5 percent from parity in the next few days after breaking the strong psychological resistance of five percent on Tuesday. 

 "Upbeat mood will keep the zloty strong and any weakening of the currency will be a good buying oportunity," said Robert Hryciuk, dealer at Bank of America Polska SA. "I think now the market sees new levels for the zloty at around 5.5 percent." 

 Dealers said the National Bank of Poland (NBP) might still refrain from forex market interventions, despite the zloty's ongoing appreciation. 

 "The central bank may stay quiet for a while to see how far the market want to push the zloty," Nomura's Bublik said. 

 "Rates are high and they are going to be attractive for some time so I don't think people are too worried about whether the central bank is really going to intervene or not. There is the natural pull for the zloty to go strong," he added. 

 On the money market one-day deposits stayed above the central bank's drainage rates of 24 percent and overnight ratwes closed the day at 24.25/24.70 against the opening's 24.50/24.70 percent.

title: Zloty hits new highs on band widening expectations.
text:
WARSAW, Feb 25 (Reuters) - The zloty jumped against the currency basket in early Wednesday trade on market expectations that the central bank's monetary policy council may widen the daily trading band and allow the unit to rise. 

 "What is happening now is a result of pure speculation as the market tries to guess what decisions the Monetary Policy Council could announce today," said Malgorzata Sawicka, senior forex dealer at Bank Handlowy SA. 

 Dealers said the central bank's Monetary Policy Council (RPP), setting monetary and exchange rate policies, may want to widen the zloty's trading band to plus/minus 15 percent from the current plus/minus seven percent. 

 "Although they could decide to extend the zloty's band, it remains to be seen whether the central bank would then let the zloty rise towards, say, four percent (from parity)," Handlowy's Sawicka said. 

 In recent weeks the National Bank of Poland has been intervening on the makret to cap the zloty's rise at around 2.2 percent firmer than the parity rate -- set daily against the basket of five western currencies and a devaluation factor. 

 At 0910 GMT the zloty hit a 10-month high at 2.94/2.91 percent firmer than the parity rate against the opening's 2.62/2.49 percent. 

 It was at 3.5220/30 to the dollar against 3.5290/40 at the start and at 1.9544/50 to the mark against 1.9640/65. 

 Dealers said potential profit-taking later in the day could limit the speculative zloty rise on Wednesday. 

 "The zloty has a chance to test even three percent from parity today if the morning madness continues, but as there were some signs of profit-taking already yesterday, the market may find its equilibrium somewhere between 2.5 and three percent," one foreign bank dealer in Warsaw said. 

 On the money market early one-day deposits inched down on Wednesday due to large cash surpluses on the market in the last days of the February reserve period. 

 "(Short-term) rates will probably continue a downward slide until the end of this reserve period as banks have plenty of cash," said Aleksandra Watroba, money market dealer at Bank Slaski SA. 

 Early overnight rates traded at 22.30/22.45 percent against the opening's 22.35/22.65 and tomorrow/next were at 22.20/22.50 against 22.35/22.65.

title: Poland's Zloty Rises Early On Strong Dollar Buying
text:
WARSAW (Dow Jones)--The Polish zloty (PLN) is higher against the dollar early Tuesday as investors continue to buy zlotys for dollars. 

 Dealers said the zloty is trading at around 2.4% above the midpoint of the trading band but said the central bank has yet to react to the market's steep climb. 

 In the last couple of weeks, the central bank has intervened to buy dollars or Deutsche marks when the zloty has reached 2.2% above the midpoint. 

 However, the zloty reached around 2.35% above the midpoint Monday and the central bank didn't intervene. 

 Around 0940 GMT, the dollar was at PLN3.5390, down from Monday's fixing of PLN3.5555. 

 The Deutsche mark was at PLN1.9665, up from Monday's fixing of PLN 1.9570. 

 Malgorzata Sawicka, dealer at Bank Handlowy, said the central bank was checking rates quoted at banks. But she said the central bank may decide to let the zloty strengthen and may not intervene. 

 Marek Cherubin, dealer at Creditanstalt, said it was hard to say why the central bank was allowing the zloty to climb but said the central bank may have decided to stop its recent wave of interventions. 

 The National Bank of Poland set the parity rate for the dollar at PLN3.6235 and for the mark at PLN2.0162. 

 The dollar is trading at 2.3% below its parity rate, and the mark is at 2.5% below its parity rate. 

 The Polish zloty is fixed to a basket of five Western currencies and is devalued at a rate of 1% per month. It is allowed to fluctuate within plus or minus 7% of the central parity rate. 

 Overnight money market rates were indicated at between 22.55% and 22.80%.

title: POLISH ZLOTY STRENGTHENS AS C.BANK STAYS QUIET.
text:
WARSAW, Feb 23 (Reuters) - The zloty gained more ground on Monday as the central bank refrained from buying currencies on the market for the second consecutive session and dealers said continued foreign flows would create more demand for the unit. 

 Over the past two weeks the National Bank of Poland (NBP) stepped in with forex market interventions nearly every day so as to cap the foreign-charged local unit's rise. 

 "It is a roulette and the central bank will keep the market guessing about its forex market intervention policy," said Rafal Petsch, forex dealer at Bank of America Polska SA. 

 Last Friday the central bank's governor said the NBP would try to fend off foreign short-term capital inflows by creating more uncertainty on the local foreign exchange market. 

 "But as the NBP did not step in today the zloty will be stronger tomorrow as foreign demand for Polish T-bills and T-bonds continues," Bank of America's Petsch said. 

 The zloty ended Monday's session at 2.34/2.28 percent from the trading band centre against Friday's 2.23/2.20 close. 

 It closed at 3.5570/85 to the dollar against 3.5595/05 on Friday and at 1.9570/85 to the mark against 1.9568/73. 

 At Monday's one billion zloty primary auction foreign investors bought an estimated $120 million worth of Polish T-bills, whose minimum prices rose sharply amid a total demand of 3.57 billion zlotys. 

 The average yield of the benchmark 52-week T-bill, mostly sought by foreign investors, fell to 21.74 percent from 22.61 percent at the previous tender last Monday. 

 Analysts said Poland's new Monetary Policy Council (RPP), which plans to hold news conference after its Wednesday morning meeting, could announce some decisions to help keep Poland's markets in balance despite the ongoing foreign capital influx. 

 "Poland is perceived as a very good place for investment and if interest rates are high and the currency relatively cheap we can expect more capital flows in the near-term," one foreign bank dealer in Warsaw said. 

 On the money market one-day depos held relatively stable on Monday and overnight rates ended the session at 22.85/23.00 against opening 22.70/23.20. Tomorrow/next ended at 22.70/22.95 against Friday's close of 21.00/22.40.

title: EARLY ZLOTY STABLE, EYES HIGHER GROUND.
text:
WARSAW, Feb 23 (Reuters) - The zloty held relatively steady in early Monday trade, but dealers said potential foreign flows into Polish Treasury-bills at Monday's primary tender may keep the currency under upward pressure later in the day. 

 "The trend for a stronger zloty remains and nothing, for now, seems to be able to undermine it. We can expect foreign capital to flow into the market," said Witold Wozniak, forex dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA. 

 Dealers expected average T-bill yields to fall to around secondary market levels at today's one billion zloty auction, with the benchmark 52-week bill seen sliding to around 21.8 percent against an average of 22.61 at the previous tender. 

 "T-bill yields will probably have to fall further, perhaps to around 20 percent, if capital flows and upward pressure on the zloty were to weaken," Deutsche's Wozniak said. 

 At 0900 GMT the zloty was at 2.24/2.21 percent from the trading band centre against the opening's 2.28/2.20 percent. 

 It was at 3.5655/65 to the dollar against 3.5641/71 at the start and at 1.9555/65 to the mark against 1.9549/64. 

 Dealers said the central bank may continue to buy foreign currencies on the domestic forex market so as to prevent a rise in the foreign-charged zloty in the near-term. 

 On Friday the National Bank of Poland (NBP) refrained from forex market interventions after buying foreign currencies at nearly every trading session for the last two weeks. 

 "With a strong currency and high interest rates it's hard to stop the foreign capital influx, but the NBP may still step in (with interventions) until longer-term steps are taken," said Jacek Wasilewski, chief dealer at Vereinsbank Polska SA. 

 Analysts expected the NBP's Monetary Policy Council (RPP), which started work last week, to discuss issues of exchange rate policy at its next meeting, scheduled for Wednesday.

title: POLISH ZLOTY WEAKENS VS BASKET, BUT MOOD UNCHANGED.
text:
WARSAW, Feb 19 (Reuters) - The zloty weakened on Thursday after the central bank bought an estimated 30 million German marks on the market but dealers said continued foreign interest in Polish treasuries would support the unit in the near-term. 

 "It will probably be a very similar day tomorrow. When the zloty firms to about 2.2 percent from parity the central bank will again step in and will try to stop its rise," said Jacek Wasilewski, chief dealer at Vereinsbank Polska SA. 

 The National Bank of Poland (NBP) twice intervened to buy marks on Thursday when the zloty firmed above 2.15 from its basket parity rate. 

 "Generally, trade here has been dull for the last few days because when banks want to make a major deal they either wait for the NBP's intervention or exchange currencies later at the fixing," Wasilewski said. 

 The zloty ended at 2.20/2.16 percent from the trading band centre against Wednesday's close of 2.25/2.21 percent. 

 It closed at 3.5585/95 to the dollar against 3.5630/40 on Wednesday and at 1.9560/70 to the mark against 1.9505/14. 

 Analysts said foreign capital would continue to seep into Polish T-bills and T-bonds, although some yields had already fallen by more than two percentage points since the start of the year. 

 The benchmark 52-week T-bill traded at around 21.80 percent in Thursday secondary trade against an average of 24.16 percent at the first primary auction this year on January 5. 

 "T-bill yields would have to fall by another two percent to make the papers unattractive," said Andrew Kenningham, analyst at Merrill Lynch in London. "When they are around 20 or 20.5 percent people may start to find them less interesting." 

 Dealers said foreign investors had also entered Polish two- and five-year fixed rate notes, which traded on Thursday around 21.40/21.10 percent and 19.80/19.30 percent respectively. 

 "So long as the central bank maintains the ceiling (on the zloty) at between 2.0 and 2.5 percent above the parity rate foreign capital will continue to flow in," Merrill Lynch's Kenningham said.

title: NEW POLISH  CENTRAL BANK  COUNCIL FACES HARD CHOICES.
text:
WARSAW, Feb 16 (Reuters) - Poland's new Monetary Policy Council will face tough decisions when it meets for the first time this week amid a flood of foreign capital which sparked central bank interventions last week, analysts said. 

 Political squabbles delayed establishment of the 10-member council responsible for monetary and exchange rate policies. This has the potential to limit the scope of central bank responses to market trends as from the start of this year. 

 In recent weeks foreign capital has poured into Poland's markets and put strong upward pressure on the zloty, forcing the central bank into currency intervention. 

 The National Bank of Poland (NBP) bought some $600 million on the domestic foreign exchange market over the last six working days alone. But its actions did little to reverse zloty gains and drew criticism from some economists. 

 "If the NBP continues with its interventions, the market will remain unbalanced, money supply and inflation will grow but the zloty will strengthen anyhow," said Krzysztof Rybinski, chief analyst at ING Barings in Warsaw. 

 Analysts said fast growing domestic demand and a large current account gap would probably keep the Monetary Policy Council (RPP) from cutting high official interest rates until at least the middle of the year. 

 "The rate of credit growth has decelerated but is still pretty high so the answer is to be conservative on rate cuts and it is not clear the economy has slowed down sufficiently yet," said Arnab Das, analyst at JP Morgan in London. 

 Analysts said the RPP was more likely to modify the exchange rate regime to make zloty investments more risky. 

 "The RPP may change its forex policy either by widening the trading band or changing day-to-day management of the forex market," JP Morgan's Das said. 

 Currently the zloty is allowed to trade within a 14 percent daily band centred on the parity rate. But the central bank has said it may expand the corridor to plus/minus 15 percent around the parity early in 1998. 

 This move may not be effective as it is the central bank's interventions which limit the actual trading band and not the outer limits of the band itself. 

 "In practice, the widening of the band will only have a psychological effect, if any. It is clear the central bank does not want the zloty to strengthen too much and will limit gains," ING's Rybinski said. 

 Analysts said the central bank could also stop announcing the daily central parity rate -- the currency's trading band mid-point -- which would make central bank intervention levels less predictable for currency speculators. 

 They said the RPP would probably also have to slow the zloty's crawling devaluation rate of one percent per month against a basket of Western currencies in the second quarter of 1998, so as to limit its inflationary effects. 

 The 1998 budget envisages a 10 percent zloty devaluation during the course of this year, which would translate into about 0.8 percent per month. But central bank officials have said that the budget figure was only indicative. 

 Analysts said a slowdown of the crawling devaluation would attract even more foreign capital to various Polish securities, which were backed by a generally healthy economy. 

 "The strength of the zloty comes from the country's sound fundamentals," said Krzysztof Bledowski, chief analyst at WoodCommerz in Warsaw. "It is a mix of soaring stock prices, high-yielding treasuries and flows from privatisation." 

 The central bank said the first RPP meeting was scheduled for February 17, the same day that Poland's president was due to appoint the final three members of the Council and his candidate for the head of the central bank. 

 The term of the current president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz expires on March 4 and a new chief has to be proposed by the president and then accepted by parliament. 

 The ruling right-wing coalition's politicians have said Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz had a very high chance of staying for a second six-year term. REUTERS

title: ZLOTY HEADS FOR WAR WITH POLISH C.BANK -ANALYSTS.
text:
WARSAW, Feb 6 (Reuters) - Recently timid foreign investors threw caution to the wind on Friday, flooding Poland's markets with capital and putting the zloty on a collision course with a central bank determined to halt its rise, analysts said. 

 Analysts said the National Bank of Poland (NBP), which bought an estimated $400 million through interventions on Friday, would be tested again over the next days as foreigners continue to flock into Poland's attractive securites. 

 "Until interest rates come down, and if the NBP continues to intervene to prevent (the zloty reaching) equilibrium levels, there is no reason why this trend cannot be sustained," said Robert Beange, economist at Lehman Brothers in London. 

 "This is always the case with inflows, that when you try to prevent what is going on then you ultimately prolong the experience," Beange added. 

 Friday's central bank intervention, one of its biggest ever, forced down the foreign-charged zloty nearly half a point against the parity rate -- the mid-point of its trading band. 

 The zloty closed at 2.07/2.01 percent on the stronger side of parity, against Thursday's close 2.50/2.46 percent. 

 Analysts said signs of recovery in Asian and other emerging markets fuelled foreign investor appetite for Poland, whose sound economic fundamentals and high rates made it one of the best investments in its risk class. 

 "Two percent is definitely a good support level for the zloty...and the recovery in Asia is continuing and that helps the currency, making it a great buy," Jesper Dannesboe, emerging market economist at ABN-Amro in London. 

 Dealers said the central bank would probably continue to intervene against the zloty in a bid to secure exports growth and keep favourable trade balance trends intact. 

 "The central bank has been consistent and today's intervention was appropriate given that Poland is not completely out of the woods in the balance of payments," said Ehsun Khan, analyst at Morgan Stanley in London. 

 Poland's current account deficit amounted to less than 3.5 percent of gross domestic product in 1997 as positive export figures late last year lowered the gap below expectations. 

 The current account gap is expected to widen to some 4.5 to 5.5 percent of GDP in 1998, analysts said. 

 Analysts said that even though Poland's Monetary Policy Council, which was supposed take control the country's monetary policy from the start of 1998, has not yet been formed, the central bank was able to take necessary measures if needed. 

 "So far five of the council's 10 members have been appointed, so together with the head of the central bank the council can make decisions if necessary," said one senior analyst at a Polish bank. 

 The central bank officials did not want to comment on the issue but the press office said that it expected the first council meeting to take place around February 17. 

 The creation of the council, which will comprise the central bank president and three members each picked by parliament's lower house, Senate and the president, has been stalled by disagreement over candidates within Poland's ruling right-centre coalition.

 Analysts said Poland's solid economic growth, a smaller than expected current account deficit in 1997 and high interest rates made the country a prime destination for capital inflows in 1998 once the storm over many emerging markets calmed.

 "It remains to be seen where the zloty's longer-term ceiling forms, but without doubt, it is not where the zloty was trading on Monday," he added. 

 Analysts said that continuing foreign demand for Polish longer-term treasuries would keep the local currency on the steady rise in the near-term.

title: POLISH  CURRENCY  LIBERALISATION IN H2 1998-FINMIN.
text:
WARSAW, Jan 28 (Reuters) - Poland's new currency law liberalising zloty trade should take effect in the second half of this year, Finance Minister Leszek Balcerowicz said on Wednesday. 

 "I think in the first half of this year the law will be adopted in parliament and in the second half there will be the major liberalisation," Balcerowicz told Reuters Financial Television in an interview. 

 The zloty is now fully convertible only domestically and cannot be used as an invoice currency in foreign trade of goods or services. 

 The bill would allow for zloty payments for goods and services purchased abroad but would keep many restrictions on capital flows and give the central bank large powers of intervention to safeguard Poland against a currency crisis. 

 Asked if the change in the currency law might make the zloty more vulnerable to a speculative attack, Balcerowicz said there were various theories. 

 "But it is beyond doubt that we have to liberalise according to our agreements with the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development and the European Union." 

 "The best response to would-be dangers is a prudent macro-economic policy and accelerated structural reforms," he added. 

 Balcerowicz, now steering a tight 1998 budget through parliament with a projected budget deficit of 1.5 percent of gross domestic product, said he hoped this would curb the flow of hot money. 

 "We are reducing the budget deficit so there is hope that the inflow of speculative capital will be less," Balcerowicz said. 

 The new centre-right government is placing priority on stabilisation of the economy after four-years of rule by the previous coalition led by ex-communists, and on pressing ahead with major privatisations and structural reforms including an overhaul of the pensions system. 

 Balcerowicz said he hoped for an inflow of foreign direct investment to Poland next year and did not think investors would be discouraged by troubles in other emerging markets. 

 "I am sure that serious investors can distinguish healthy tigers from sick tigers and I would include Poland's economy among the healthy tigers," he said.

title: POLISH C.BANK TALK LIFTS ZLOTY TO 7-WEEK HIGH.
text:
WARSAW, Dec 16 (Reuters) - The Polish zloty jumped to a seven-week high on Tuesday on the latest National Bank of Poland (NBP) verbal intervention aimed at keeping the skittish local forex market just out-of-balance, analysts said. 

 In a Tuesday newspaper deputy NBP chief Witold Kozinski said the zloty's crawling devaluation could be cut as early as February if fiscal spending remained in check, giving the unit a shot in the arm and lifiting it nearly to the parity rate. 

 "The central bank is sending the market mixed signals. The crawling peg cut is a positive factor, which offsets an earlier comment about widening the zloty's trading band and increasing risk," said Andrzej Ladko, chief dealer at Bank Handlowy SA. 

 On Tuesday the zloty was fixed at 0.05 percent below the trading band centre -- the parity rate -- up from 0.87 percent on Monday and Friday's fixing at 1.16 percent below parity. 

 On the market it closed at 0.05/0.11 percent below parity or at 3.5340/60 to the dollar, against against 3.5505/20 on Monday and at 1.9830/40 per mark, against Monday's 2.0015/20. 

 Last week the NBP said it would soon expand the zloty's trading band to plus/minus 15 percent around the mid-point from the present seven percent on either side of parity, sending the zloty sharply lower. 

 Analysts said, however, that in the end it would be capital flows which would determine zloty sentiment and that they would be driven by Poland's fundementals and the authorities' ability to keep the growing current account deficit in check. 

 They said fund managers were now sitting on positions and waiting for the end of the year, especially if they fulfilled investment requirements for 1997, but that they would again look for places to invest their money early next year. 

 "I wouldn't now be surprised if there was an inflow in January and the zloty was pushed up above the parity, even far above the parity. Especially if the trading band was expanded," said Andrew Kenningham, analyst at Merrill Lynch in London. 

 Analysts said that statements such as the International Monetary Fund's Tuesday assessment of Poland's current account defcit, which it saw under four percent of gross domestic product this year and under six percent in 1998, would also help keep the zloty strong in months to come. 

 Traders said that speculation by foreign players, which has recently played a leading large role on the thin Polish foreign exchange market, has slowed after the central bank fixed the zloty about half a percent above market level last week. 

 "The sentiment for the zloty is positive even though speculation has faded before the end of 1997 as Polish corporates are net zloty buyers in the late stages of the year," said Rafal Petsch, trader at Bank of America in London.

title: POLISH NEW  CURRENCY  LAW IN NEXT FEW MONTHS -FINMIN.
text:
WARSAW, Dec 15 (Reuters) - Poland's new currency law further liberalising zloty trade should be in place in the next few months, Finance Minister Leszek Balcerowicz said. 

 "The outline of the law is ready and it is ( the implementation) is a question of the next few months," Balcerowicz told Reuters in a Monday interview. 

 The zloty is now fully convertible only domestically and cannot be used as an invoice currency in foreign trade of goods or services. 

 The new bill would allow for zloty payments for goods and services purchased abroad but would keep many restrictions on capital flows and give the central bank large powers of intervention to safeguard Poland against a currency crisis. 

 Asked if the liberalisation of the currency law would not make the zloty more vulnerable to a speculative attack, Balcerowicz said: 

 "Not if we retain control over the liberalisation. What's more, the liberalisation is another reason why we should conduct stable macroeconomic policies." 

 Balcerowicz's cabinet has set the stabilisation of the economy after a four-year rule of the previous ex-communist and peasant coalition as its main task for next year. It has said that the previous government did not take advantage of the fast growth to complete market reforms and encouraged living beyond one's means. 

 Balcerowicz said he expected a large inflow of foreign direct investment to Poland next year as Western enterpreneurs appreciate the country's sound economic fundamentals against less impressive performance of other emerging markets.

title: Poland  Central Bank /Zloty Band -3: Deval Rate Unchanged
text:
Kozinski said a 30-point band for the zloty - 15 points on either side of the midpoint - would conform to practice in the European Union. 

 He said a wider band would result in greater volatility of the exchange rate and thus increase the uncertainty for investors in short-term zloty instruments. 

 'The psychological effect will be such, that investors won't be certain of their gains, because the (National Bank of Poland) will have much more scope for intervention,' Kozinski is quoted as saying. 

 Kozinski said he expects an inflow of foreign currency into Poland's short-term Treasury bill market in January. A wider trading band, and greater currency volatility, could stem that inflow, he said. 

 The central bank is worried about such inflows because foreign money attracted by high domestic interest rates puts upward pressure on the zloty, making Polish goods less competitive abroad and widening the trade deficit. 

 Inflows of foreign currency also pump up the money supply, making it more difficult for the central bank to fight inflation through open-market operations. 

 Kozinski said he didn't expect the monthly rate of devaluation to be reduced as long as domestic interest rates remain high. The Polish currency is currently devalued at a rate of 1% a month. 

 He said any decision on a change in the rate of zloty devaluation would depend on maintaining a tight fiscal policy.

title: Poland Zloty Gains Midday, But  Central Bank  Stands Aside
text:
WARSAW (AP-Dow Jones)--The Polish zloty has regained some ground midday Thursday after being down slightly against the currency basket earlier in the session. 

 The National Bank of Poland again confounded expectations by failing to intervene for the second straight day, even as the zloty approached the level of 1% above the midpoint of the trading band. 

 Around 1045 GMT, the dollar was at 3.4010 zlotys, down from 3.4015 zlotys at the opening and from Wednesday's fixing of 3.4050 zlotys.

 Dealers said the central bank had given up trying to keep the zloty from rising to more than 0.5% above the midpoint of the band. They said 1% above the midpoint may constitute a new intervention level. 

 'If we don't reach 1% today, then the central bank won't enter the market,' said Malgorzata Sawicka, a trader at Bank Handlowy. 'The central bank has decided to give us some freedom.' 

 But she and other dealers predicted the central bank would intervene at some point as the zloty continues to move up against the basket, buoyed by foreign purchases of Polish securities. 

 Sawicka said news that former Finance Minister Leszek Balcerowicz may become deputy prime minister for economic affairs in the new government had given the zloty a boost. His appointment, she said, would further strengthen the currency.

 The Polish zloty is fixed to a basket of five Western currencies and is devalued at a rate of 1% per month. It is allowed to fluctuate within plus or minus 7% of the central parity rate.

text:
The central bank intervened when the zloty rose more than 0.5% above the midpoint of its trading band against a basket of Western currencies. 

 Even though the zloty is theoretically allowed to fluctuate within a 14-point band around the midpoint, the central bank has now established an informal cap of 0.5% on the strong side of the midpoint, dealers said. 

 If not for the intervention, the zloty could move up more than 1% above the midpoint, said Piotr Czyzewski, a dealer at ING Bank. 'It has the strength,' he said. 

 Monday's intervention was relatively mild and 'only slightly weakened the zloty,' said Wlodzimierz Osak, a dealer at Bank Polska Kasa Opieki SA. The result, he said, was a 'cosmetic correction' to the zloty's upward trend. 

 The central bank, participants said, is worried that a sudden influx of foreign capital seeking high yields on Polish government securities is pushing up the zloty at a time when the widening trade deficit is causing alarm. 

 If the Polish currency gains too much, the reasoning goes, Poland's external balances could deteriorate further, eventually leading to a sudden withdrawal of foreign capital and a rapid depreciation of the currency. 

 The appetite of foreign investors for Polish securities was whetted by the Sept. 21 Parliamentary election, in which Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) defeated the ruling Democratic Left Alliance (SLD).

title: Poland Zloty Seen Rising Further On Coalition Hopes
text:
WARSAW (AP-Dow Jones)--The Polish zloty took a wild ride on Monday in reaction to Sunday's election results, but dealers said the outlook is positive. 

 They said favorable reaction to the election victory by Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) and strong foreign demand for Polish securities should push up the zloty in coming days. 

 'The market is optimistically inclined toward the zloty,' said Jaroslaw Krol, a dealer at ABN Amro bank. 

 The zloty gained sharply in early dealing Monday morning following news that AWS had defeated the ruling Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) in the parliamentary election. 

 Market participants were particularly heartened by the strong third-place finish of the reform-minded Freedom Union (UW) party and by the likelihood that UW would form a coalition with AWS, thus tempering that party's trade-unionist tendencies. 

 But later on Monday morning Polish banks, expecting central bankintervention to damp the zloty's rise and hoping to ride the dollar's rise against the Deutsche mark, started selling the Polish currency, dealers said. 

 When the National Band of Poland finally intervened to buy dollars at the level of 3.4370 zlotys, the zloty was already on its way down, dealers said.
