title: Polish rate cut seen in December, maybe Wednesday.
text:
WARSAW, Dec 8 (Reuters) - Poland's Monetary Council (RPP) is expected to trim interest rates by at least 100 bp in December, but analysts are divided whether the policy making body will make its move as soon as this Wednesday, when it meets. 

 Analysts said on Tuesday that falling inflation and slower economic growth pointed toward an interest rate cut in the near-term, but some expected the 10-member council to hold off decisions until its next meeting on December 16. 

 "I expect a 100 basis point cut in the intervention rate on Wednesday and no changes in official rates," said Krzysztof Rybinski, chief economist at ING Barings in Warsaw. 

 The 28-day money-market drainage rate, called the intervention rate, is now set at a minimum of 17 percent. 

 Official rates, which the central bank said reflected longer-term policy trends, now stand at 22 percent for the lombard and 20 percent for the discount rate. 

 Other analysts expected more drastic rate cuts. 

 "The likelihood is greater that they will move on the 16th rather than tomorrow and my forecast is for about a 200 basis point cut," said Juliet Sampson, currency strategist at Bank of America in London. 

 A Reuters poll released on Tuesday showed 20 of Poland's 21 largest banks expected a cut in the intervention rate and 13 banks saw a cut in the lombard rate this month. 

 Analysts said financial markets have mostly priced in the widely-expected loosening, with the zloty slipping in recent days while stocks regained ground lost in November. 

 "About 100 basis points have been priced in already and if there is a 200 bp cut then we could see the zloty slip a touch," Bank of America's Sampson said. She added her year-end target for the zloty was 3.55 to the dollar. 

 On Tuesday the zloty was at 3.5095 to the dollar and at 2.0995 to the mark, or 6.19 percent above its trading band mid-point. The zloty can fluctuate in a band of 12.5 percent on either side of its parity rate centre. 

 Warsaw shares eased 0.4 percent to 12,227 points on Tuesday but remain six percent higher than at the start of December. Analysts said the Tuesday easing was due to profit taking after sharp gains in anticipation of the rate cut. 

 Analysts said interest rate cuts must accompany falls in inflation to keep Poland's economic engine, hurt by the collapse of Russia and slowing growth in the EU, in high gear. 

 Finance Minister Leszek Balcerowicz expects the economy to grow five percent in 1999, but most analysts are not as upbeat. 

 "The slowing of economic growth can be quite extensive next year, especially over the first two quarters. Overall GDP should grow 4.5 percent against 5.5 percent in 1998," said Krzysztof Bledowski, chief economist at WoodCommerz in Warsaw. 

 (C) Reuters Limited 1998.

WARSAW, Nov 10 (Reuters) - The buoyant zloty hit a new three-month high early on Tuesday, breaching a psychological level of 8.0 percent above the parity rate amid improving investment prospects in emerging markets, dealers said. 

 At 0940 GMT the zloty firmed to 8.11/8.07 percent above the parity rate against the opening 8.09/7.98 percent and Monday's 8.01 percent fix. 

 It traded at 3.4380/95 to the dollar against 3.4360/00 at the start and at 2.0350/60 to the mark agianst 2.0370/00. 

 The zloty last traded above 8.0 percent stronger than parity in mid-August before its was engulfed by Russia's economic and political crisis, during which it plunged below its trading band mid-point. 

 "Improved sentiment on emerging markets seems the main factor behind the zloty's rise. It was partly due to foreign buying, although foreign traders are less active today," said Piotr Lancucki, currency dealer at BNP-Dresdner in Warsaw. 

 Analysts said that recent gains on many markets and an expected mulit-billion dollar bail-out aid package for Brasil has lifted hopes for economic stability in emerging markets. 

 One-year Non-Delivery Forwards (NDFs) dipped to 14.2/14.7 on Tuesday against Monday's 14.5/15.1 percent, signalling some foreign entry into zloty instruments, dealers said. 

 The market did not expect the National Bank of Poland (NBP) to step in with dollar-buying interventions for the time being to curb the zloty's appreciation. 

 "Very probably the NBP will stay away from the market until the zloty approaches 10 percent. The band was widened so they have no need to defend it at the moment," a forex dealer said. 

 In late October the central bank's Monetary Policy Council widened the zloty's band to plus/minus 12.5 percent on either side of a parity rate from the previous plus/minus 10 percent. 

 The zloty's parity rate is now gradually devalued at a pace of 0.5 percent per month to neutralise Poland's high inflation. ((Pawel Kozlowski, Warsaw Newsroom, tel. +48 22 653 9700, fax +48 22 653 9780, warsaw.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Poland's zloty regains all Russian crisis losses.
text:
WARSAW, Nov 2 (Reuters) - The Polish zloty climbed back to heights not seen since before Russia's collapse in mid-August, rekindling expectations of central bank interventions against the local currency. 

 The zloty jumped to 7.28 percent above its trading band centre on Monday from Friday's 6.63 percent - its highest level since August 17 when Russia devalued the rouble. 

 Since the rouble's demise the zloty, which can trade in a band of 12.5 percent on either side of its parity mid-point, touched lows below the central rate and stayed volatile before starting a gradual uptrend some four weeks ago. 

 Analysts said the zloty's gains were fuelled by large privatisations that brought capital into the country and by the recent improvement in sentiment on global markets. 

 "External factors that weighed heavy on the zloty seemingly disappeared. Surely (problems in) Brasil and Russia still exist but when things there are calm, the zloty bounces back to pre-crises levels," said Zbigniew Chmielewski, chief dealer at ING Barings in Warsaw. 

 Analysts said the central bank, worried about the effects of the stronger zloty on Poland's deteriorating current account balance, could start buying dollars on the foreign exchange market if the local currency firms much further. 

 "The zloty should quickly return to nine or ten percent above parity unless the National Bank of Poland (NBP) starts to intervene in the meantime," Chmielewski said. 

 "Once the zloty tops eight percent they may start thinking about interventions, but such actions would only slow, not end, the further appreciation of the zloty," he added. 

 The NBP last intervened on the local forex market in July. 

 Analysts said Germany's Bayerische HypoVereinsbank's one billion mark aquisition of a 37 percent stake in Poland's Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA (BPH) and the privatisation of telecoms giant TPSA have kept the market under zloty-buying pressure over the last several weeks. 

 But portfolio capital flows were not expected to return as quickly because many investors had been badly burned by the Russian crisis. 

 "FDI and privatisation inflows have pushed the zloty higher with only limited help from porftolio inflows as many foreign players are still licking their wounds after Russia," said Rafal Petsch, senior dealer at Bank of America in Warsaw. 

 Treasury yields also felt the impact of the strengthening zloty and sharp reduction in the Finance Ministry's offer, with the benchmark 52-week T-bill down to 14.12 percent at Monday's auction from 17.15 percent in early September. 

 The Ministry cut this month's T-bill offer by a third from October to only 2.2 billion zlotys over five primary tenders. 

 Analysts said disappointing current account data, which in September alone amounted to about $1.2 billion, could turn sentiment against the zloty if it was sustained. 

 Over the first eight months of the year Poland had a $2.42 billion C/A deficit, or about $300 per month, against a $4.27 billion shortfall in all of 1997 which amounted to 3.2 percent of gross domestic product.

title: INSTANT VIEW - Polish RPP cuts interest rates.
text:
WARSAW, Oct 28 (Reuters) - Poland's Monetary Policy Council (RPP) lowered the lombard rate by two percentage points to 22 percent and the main 28-day market intervention rate by one percent to a minimum of 17 percent as of October 29. 

 The RPP cut the discount rate by 1.5 percentage points to 20.0 percent and also widened the zloty's daily fluctuation band to plus/minus 12.5 percent from the parity rate from the previous plus/minus 10 percent limit. 

 Following are analysts' reactions to the decisions: 

 WIKE GROENENBERG, ECONOMIST AT SALOMON, SMITH & BARNEY 

 "The decision to lower interest rates doesn't come as a surprise. It reflects the sharp decline in inflation over the last few months, the slowing in the economic growth rate, as well as the firming of the zloty. What is somewhat surprising is that the central bank has also decided to widen the band. I think they are doing this because they want to create more scope for the zloty to appreciate. Poland has become an area of interest for investors as they are betting on longer-term convergence. 

 "A cut of 100 basis points was very much discounted, so I think the currency will remain firm or to strengthen further. In the longer run the monetary authorities want to increase the risk premium for foreigners investing in Poland and widening the band is part of this policy." 

 ZSOLT PAPP, SBC WARBURG 

 "I think it was definitely a good move. If you look at the economic data, it certainly justified the decision to cut interest rates. Real interest rates are still relatively high, so there is no actual risk. If you look at the situation on financial markets, it seemed to justify it too. The zloty has been strengthening quite sharply over the last few weeks. It was probably the right time to take some pressure out of it. 

 "Because everybody was expecting the rate cut, if they hadn't cut now, it could have backfired. The rate cut should have been largely priced in, but I think in the short term the zloty could even strengthen further, because the decision signals confidence. The economy is growing, inflation is coming down, the current account deficit is not a problem, they are also not that afraid of external impact. The band widening that comes with it is also a signal that the national bank is preparing for more convertibility of the zloty. But in the longer run the zloty should probably ease again over the next few months." 

 SONJA GIBBS, NOMURA, LONDON 

 "I do think at least here in London many people were looking for a little bit more off the intervention rate, particularly in light of all the indicators in Poland which have really supported the case for lower interest rates. A little bit of disappointment there on the intervention rate and prospects of continued zloty strength. 

 "I think the widening in the band was perhaps expected a little bit futher on, but the zloty has been seeing quite a lot in terms of capital inflow, which has really been supporting the currency to the point where plus/minus 10 percent starts to look as if it was not quite enough, especially on the upside. So by doing this and by not quite cutting the intervention rate as much as it has been expected what you probably see is more zloty strength pushing toward the upper end of this range. 

 "The case for rate reduction in Poland is so clear...that we could look for more cuts there, probably another 200 basis points before the end of the year." 

 JOHN LOMAX, ANALYST AT HSBC JAMES CAPEL 

 "I think it's moderately good news in the sense that the key 28-day rate was cut pretty much in line with expectation. The lombard and the discount rates were cut more agressively. As important is the widening of the trading band to 12.5 percent. The aim there seems to have been two-fold. First, it should deter speculative capital from coming into Poland, and secondly, the widening of the band actually gives the RPP some scope to keep real interest rates higher for longer without running into any exchange rate constraints. 

 "I imagine the stock market will take the news moderately well, not hugely well, since a lot of this had already been discounted after the cabinet approved the budget." 

 ((Warsaw Newsroom, tel. +48 22 653 9700,

title: Russia crisis will not change Polish policy - RPP.
text:
WARSAW, Sept 9 (Reuters) - Poland's Monetary Policy Council (RPP) said on Wednesday it would not change the course of its interest rate and forex policy because of the crisis in Russia. 

 "Taking into consideration Poland's solid fundamentals, the RPP believes it is justified to continue the present course of changes in monetary policy, including exchange rate and interest rate policy," central bank chief Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz told a news conference. 

Poland's decision-making RPP cut its 28-day market intervention rate to a minimum of 18 percent from the earlier floor of 19 percent. 

 It also slowed the rate of zloty's monthly devaluation to 0.5 percent against a currency basket from the previous 0.65 percent a month. 

 Over the last six months the central bank's RPP council has repeatedly lowered both market and official interest rates and slowed the pace of the zloty's devaluation. ((Wojciech Moskwa, Warsaw Newsroom, tel. +48 22 653 9700, fax +48 22 653 9780, warsaw.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Zloty passed test by surviving Russia crisis - RPP.
text:
WARSAW, Sept 9 (Reuters) - The Polish zloty's recent rebound from sharp losses in the wake of the Russian crisis showed the local currency was strong, said Boguslaw Grabowski, a member of Poland's decision-making Monetary Policy Council. 

 On Wednesday the zloty was fixed around 3.57 percent above its trading band mid-point, up from about even with parity at the height of the crisis in Russia in late August. 

 Before the crisis the zloty traded around 9.0 percent above the parity rate, dangerously near the upper end of its trading band of plus/minus 10 percent from parity. 

 "The zloty passed the test, its depreciation was small looking at the scale of disturbances on world markets," Grabowski told Reuters. 

 "It is important that the process of depreciation stopped and rebounded without any type of intervention from the central bank," he told Reuters after a Council meeting which cut the country's main market intervention rate by one percent. 

Poland's zloty moves within a range of 10 percent above or below a parity rate set each day by the central bank. 

 Zloty parity is determined by the value of a basket of five Western currencies against which the unit is devalued at a rate of 0.50 percent per month. ((Wojciech Moskwa, Warsaw Newsroom, tel. +48 22 653 9700, fax +48 22 653 9780, warsaw.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Wrap/Polish Zloty -2: Supportive Words From  Central Bank
text:
Although Poland's central bank opted not to intervene directly to support the zloty Friday, several officials made statements intended to soothe investors and to lend the currency some verbal support. 

 "There is no reason to worry," said Dariusz Rosati, a member of the Monetary Policy Council. "These type of big swings that we've seen in the last two days aren't something pleasant, but they don't worry me because they aren't a symptom of any serious disease on our side." 

 With the zloty hovering around its parity rates against the dollar and Deutsche mark, Rosati said there was no reason for central bankintervention. However, he said the central bank may move to "smooth" market volatility if necessary. 

 Because Russia accounts for less than 10% of Polish trade volume, the Polish economy won't suffer from the devaluation of the ruble, said Deputy Finance Minister Jaroslaw Bauc. 

 "If the crisis continues in Russia, there will be some effects on the real sphere in Poland, but I wouldn't panic," Bauc said. He said the prospect of rising interest rates and an economic slowdown in Western Europe posed a greater threat. 

 Already, some adventurous investors are starting to cautiously build up zloty positions, taking advantage of what they see as temporary weakness, analysts said.

title: Zloty rides to new record high, nears top of band.
text:
WARSAW, Aug 4 (Reuters) - The zloty ripped through strong resistance at nine percent above parity on Tuesday to close at a new record high as more foreign money poured into Poland. 

 The zloty closed at 9.08/9.03 percent above the parity rate, bettering Monday's record close of 8.89/8.84 percent and nearing the top of its daily fluctuation band of plus/minus 10 percent on either side of the parity rate centre. 

 The National Bank of Poland did not intervene on the local market for the second day running on Tuesday, after buying some $200 million last week to cool the zloty. This gave the Polish unit time to gather upward momentum, dealers said. 

 "The zloty is hot. We should see more gains tomorrow and without central bank interventions, the market could even test the 10 percent trading band limit," said a senior forex dealer at a foreign bank in Warsaw. 

 Other players said the zloty could slip from record highs amid light profit-taking after going so far in past weeks. 

 "We will probably see some profit-taking soon...but unless something fundamental changes in Poland, you can see the zloty trading well above eight percent," said Ryszard Bublik, trader at Nomura International in London. 

 The zloty closed at 3.4320/40 per dollar, against 3.4390/05 on Monday, and at 1.9246/56 to the mark, against 1.9255/65. 

 Foreigners were interested in zloty debt because the country's rates were still high in real terms, making it a good convergence play as Poland seeks EU accession, and because further rate cuts were expected still in 1998, analysts said. 

 The central bank would not be able to continue to carry out costly forex market interventions over the longer term, so a pre-emptive rate cut could be in the works, they added. 

 "It will be very interesting to see how the (decision-making) RPP monetary policy council reacts to the zloty's rise when it meets on August 19," Nomura's Bublik said. 

 The zloty's trading band centre - the parity rate - is set each day by the central bank according to the value of a basket of five Western currencies and a devaluation factor. 

 The currency's parity depreciates by 0.65 percent per month against a basket to help keep Poland's exports competitive in a context of double-digit domestic inflation. 

 Wednesday's 700 million zloty fixed rate T-bond tender should receive a warm welcome from paper-hungry foreign investors despite an expected fall of several percentage points in yields, dealers said. 

 "The secondary market is depleted and clients want size, meaning they will want to buy at the tender," said Wlodzimierz Kado, dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

title: Polish trade gap takes wind from zloty's sails.
text:
WARSAW, Sept 13 (Reuter) - The Polish zloty, long under appreciation pressure as a result of the country's huge current account surplus, is losing its upward thrust as the surplus fades with little hope of returning in full force. 

 Economists said cross-border trade inflows, which financed the trade gap and kept the zloty up in the past, were too small to offset the ever-larger merchandise trade deficit. 

 In the first seven months of this year imports soared by more than 30 percent against the same period of 1995, while exports have grown by only 10 percent and cross-border trade inflows remained virutally unchanged. 

 "Cross-border trade is still there, but currency inflows generated by it are not as noticable on the forex market as before," said Andrzej Kopec, chief dealer at Bank Slaski SA. 

 Poland had a minute $10 million current account deficit in the January-July period, compared to a $3.2 billion surplus in the corresponding period of 1995. 

 Economists said the current account balance deteriorated because of the more than 10 percent real-term appreciation of the zloty over the last year, as well as the need for imports, especially investment imports by the emerging economy. 

 "The drastic appreciation pressure on the zloty will not return," said Adam Czyzewski of the independent NOBE institute. 

 "Current account flows have balanced and large-scale speculative foreign investment inflows in treasuries have ended," Czyzewski added. 

 Throughout 1995 and early this year the National Bank of Poland was forced to intervene on the forex makret to keep the zloty from strengthening, but fading appreciation pressure has kept the central bank silent since May. 

 During the last three months the zloty has weakened more than one percent against its basket of five western currencies within its 14-percent daily trading band. 

 The band's mid-point -- the parity rate -- is set daily by the central bank according to the value of the basket, comprised mainly of the dollar and the mark and a crawling peg devaluation factor, currently at one percent per month. 

 "It's basically an importers market now and strong zloty aprreciation pressure is gone," said Malgorzata Sawicka, senior dealer at Bank Handlowy SA. 

 Some analysts said the zloty may continue to depreciate in the coming months as Belarus and Russia begin to implement controls on cross-border traders, curbing hard currency flows. 

 The government, however, seems intent on keeping the zloty edging up in real terms in the next several years, which would likely require cutting the devaluation factor in line with falling inflation. 

 The finance ministry and the International Monterary Fund (IMF) have signalled this week that Poland should consider more flexibility in its exchange rate policy. 

 "While the crawling peg regime had served Poland well in the past, (the IMF) generally considered that a more flexible exchange rate policy could increase the effectiveness of monetary policy and bring about lower inflation," the IMF said in a report released on Friday. 

 Finance Minister Grzegosz Kolodko said he envisiged a 4.3 percent real-term appreciation of the zloty next year but did not specify how this would be achieved. 

 "Poland needs to find a balanced course for zloty appreciation, so exports are not badly damaged but inflation remains headed downward," said Aleksander Welfe, head of the independent LIFEA economic think-tank.

 Around 0830 GMT, the dollar was at 2.6912 zlotys, up from 2.6893 zlotys at the opening but down from Thursday's fixing of 2.6930 zlotys.

title: OUTLOOK-ZLOTY EYES T-BILL TENDER, YIELDS SEEN FLAT.
text:
WARSAW, May 24 (Reuter) - The weekly Polish T-bill auction is seen oversubscribed on Monday but analysts expected yields to stay flat because of a likely small foreign interest due to a banking holiday in London. 

 "I expect total demand to be 1.3 to 1.4 billion zlotys at the tender, but foreign interest is likely to be weak because of the holiday in London, which should help keep maximum yields flat," said Bartlomiej Kumela of Societe Generale. 

 Analysts saw demand at the 900-million-zloty auction focused on the longest offered paper the 39-week bill -- in the absence of the benchmark 52-week bill and the 26-week paper. 

 They said however, that after a quiet Monday, foreigners should return on Tuesday buying T-bill on the secondary market. 

 "That is also why Polish banks are likely to boost bids at the primary tender, because they hope to sell it on the market later in the week," one dealer at a foreign bank here said. 

 At the last two auctions foreigners bought a total of about $70 million worth of Polish T-bills. 

 Analysts expected the maximum yield of the 39-week paper at the primary tender unchanged at 21.10 percent. 

 They said small foreign presence at the Monday tender should also keep the local foreign exchange market quiet, but some expected zloty swings on Tuesday. 

 "Monday is likely to be quiet because of the London holiday, but some foreign T-bill buying is likely to stir up trade on Tuesday, though much depends on how the central bank will take it," said Krzysztof Kozuchowski of Bank Handlowy SA. 

 This week the National Bank of Poland stepped in heavily with estimated $80-90 million interventions on Wednesday to stop the zloty's rise above three percent from the parity rate -- the centre of the daily 14-petrect trading band. 

 The NBP buying was the first in weeks as the bank let the zloty rally whenever foreigners were buying Polish paper to diminish their profit with an unfavourable exchnage rate. 

 The bank has said it was not keen on short-term foreign investment in Polish paper because the currency inflows created problems in managing its money supply. 

 The Wednesday interventions set the zloty back to about 2.5 percent from parity and dealers said foreign investor withdrawal from the sagging Warsaw bourse kept the market bearish on the zloty on Friday. 

 The NBP fixed the Polish currency at 2.6935 against the dollar down from 2.6680 a week ago and 1.7455 against the mark, also down from 1.7430 last Friday. 

 Dealers expected demand at the Tuesday 374 million zloty one-year floating bond auction to be under 250 million zlotys, because the ministry's decision to remove the five-percent- above-inflation premium from the paper made it unattractive. 

 "With the premium gone, banks are likely to bid with deep discounts, at 96.5-98.5, because the paper is less attractive than a 52-week T-bill," said Pawel Dudzinski of Pekao SA. 

 At the last tender of the paper, which has a coupon equal to year-on-year inflation two months before maturity, the minimum price was 96.67 and the average was 99.57.

title: Outlook for Polish T-bills mixed after April CPI.
text:
WARSAW, May 17 (Reuter) - Poland's April inflation data is likely to set off a price tug-of-war at the Monday primary T-bill tender as investors were mixed as to how the figures should influence yields in the near-term, analysts said. 

 The Central Statistical Office said on Friday consumer prices grew 2.2 percent in April after a 1.5 percent rise in March taking the year-on-year index down to 20.3 percent from March's 20.4 percent. 

 "The April data could be better, but it is not bad either -- the trend, after all, is down in year-on-year terms," said Pawel Wolczynski of ING bank. 

 "I would expect the benchmark maximum yield to ease slightly to 21.00 or 20.99 percent from 21.05 at the last tender, with the average maybe down to 20.95 percent from 20.98," he said. 

 But others said the larger-than-expected April price rise was unlikely to inspire banks to pay more for the paper as the government inflation target of 17 percent in December became less and less realistic. 

 "The inflation figures were rather uninspiring and I would see the benchmark average yield up at about 21.00 percent," said Wojciech Kowalczyk of Bank Handlowy SA. 

 Dealers said foreign investors could enter the auction at a level similar to last Monday, when they placed an estimated $70 million in Polish paper. 

 They expected total demand at the one-billion zloty auction to be about 1.5 billion zlotys. 

 "I don't think CPI figures, however they are interpreted, will keep foreigners away for long -- if they don't show up in large number on Monday, they will come at the next tender," said Pawel Gajewski of Creditanstalt SA. 

 Dealers said the expected foreign entry in Polish T-bills should keep the zloty bullish early in the week. 

 They said the National Bank of Poland was unlikely to intervene against the zloty because it wanted to deter short-term foreign investment in Polish paper to limit the inflationary impulse from fast currency reserve growth. 

 "The central bank wants to cut foreign profit on Polish T-bills by letting the zloty rise, so I would not expect interventions early in the week," said Creditanstalt's Gajewski. 

 However, some dealers said the dollar's expected rise on world market's might make any central bank action unnecessary. 

 "The dollar is seen rising to about 1.54 marks next week, which could take the zloty down to about up to 2.6800 against the dollar," said Marcin Trzykowski of Bank Pekao SA. @ 

 Analysts said players want to keep the zloty between 2.5 and 2.9 percent from the average weighted dollar and mark parity rate -- the centre of the daily trading band -- sailing between the market's bullish zloty mood and the NBP's favoured level of 2.5 percent. 

 "The zloty is likely to be quoted at about 2.7 percent from the parity rate next week," Pekao's Trzykowski said.

title: Polish  central bank  steps in to stop zloty rise.
text:
WARSAW, March 20 (Reuter) - The National Bank of Poland intervened against the zloty just before the market closed Wednesday, reaffirming it had no intention of letting the Polish currency strengthen in the near term, dealers said. 

 "The central bank stepped in to show that it would not let the zloty rise in the near term," said Mateusz Bieniek of Societe Generale. 

 Dealers reported a clear dollar selling trend in the market today on possible renewed foreign buying of Polish T-bills amid growing expectations of an interest rate cut. 

 "The market sentiment has long been in favour of the zloty but today it could have been augmented by some foreign entry into Polish T-bills," said Bieniek. 

 To stop the Polish currency, which had been creeping up against a basket of currencies since opening, the NBP bought an estimated $30 million on the market through a series of interventions ranging from 2.5741 zlotys through 2.5748 zlotys. 

 The interventions started when the zloty moved up to 2.56 percent from weighted dollar and mark parity rate -- the centre of the daily 14-percent trading band -- and was brought back to a previous NBP-establised level of 2.53 percent. 

 Dealers said renewed foreign interest in Polish paper, although not large, was likely to have been influenced by better-than-expected February inflation data which spurred expectations of a near-term interest rate cut. 

 Inflation last month was 1.5 percent against the expected 1.8 percent and January's 3.4 percent, which took the year-on-year index down to 20.4 percent from 21.2 in January. 

 "There is no big rush from foreigners yet, but we might see more of them at the next primary T-bill auction on Monday because February inlation data spurred rate cut expectations," said Piotr Bednarek of ING bank in Warsaw. 

 Some analysts expected the NBP could cut its discount and lombard rates, now at 23 and 26 percent respectively by about one point in response to the consumer price data. 

 "I expect a one point interest rate cut very soon as the NBP promised to have smaller but more frequent rate moves in line with falling inflation," said Barbara Kowalczyk, analyst at Bank Gdanski SA. 

 Dealers said Poland's current account data, which showed a surplus if cross-border inflows were taken into consideration, would keep the zloty testing the NBP intervention levels for weeks to come. 

 "Cash flow data shows demand for the zloty is rising and banks will keep testing NBP levels in the weeks, eventually forcing the zloty up -- maybe to three percent from parity," said Jan Mieczkowski, treasurer at Deutsche Bank here. 

 However, some dealers said the NBP could keep the zloty at 2.5 percent from the parity rate until the third quarter of this year. 

 -- Jan Strupczewski +48 22 653 9700

title: FOCUS - POLISH NBP CAPS ZLOTY'S NEAR-TERM GROWTH.
text:
WARSAW, March 13 (Reuter) - The National Bank of Poland (NBP) awoke from a weeks-long slumber today and intervened on the interbank forex market to stop the zloty's rise against the dollar and the mark, analysts said on Wednesday. 

 Analysts said the central bank's dollar buying operation did not attempt to weaken the zloty, but to re-establish the Polish unit's past resistance levels in case banks forgot about them during several weeks of more balanced trade. 

 The zloty was stopped when it rose to 2.53 percent from the dollar and mark parity rate -- the centre of the daily 14-percent trading band -- with a symbolic $10 million purchase at 2.5690 zlotys. 

 Analysts said however, the zloty's upward probe and the subsequent central bank action came as no surprise to the market, saturated with currencies from huge cross-border trade inflows. 

 The unregistered trade was estimated to contribute some $6 billion to Poland's currency reserves last year. 

 "The NBP wanted to show the market that the zloty's past resistance levels are still well guarded," said Przemyslaw Ciszecki, senior forex dealer at ING bank in Warsaw. 

 Analysts said today's intervention level was likely to serve as the zloty's near-term ceiling and that the central bank would need to purchase more dollars from the market if it wanted to keep the zloty from strengthening in the longer-term. 

 "The zloty's appreciation in the future is inevitable," said Jan Mieczkowski, treasurer at Deutsche Bank Polska. 

 Analysts said the zloty was now likely spend a next week or two hovering around the intervention level of 2.5 percent from the parity rate and occasionally stab at resistance. 

 However, analysts said the zloty had a very weak short-term support and could be volitile if the market was rapidly flooded with zlotys, as was the case in February when foreign investors took profits on parts of their Polish T-bill portfolios. 

 "Another wave of withdrawing foreign investors could easily reverse the zloty's natural upward inclination in the short-term," one forex dealer at a foreign bank here said. 

 Last month investors began to sell Polish T-bills as yields started to bottom out after an early January interest rate cut and the ensuing four point drop in T-bill yields. 

 On Wednesday the zloty was fixed at an average of 2.52 percent from the parity rate at 2.5685 to the dollar and at 1.7460 to the mark. 

 The Polish currency is devalued one percent per month against a basket of currencies comprised of the U.S. dollar and the German mark as well as the British pound and Swiss and French francs. 

 -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700

 Dealers estimated that today's National Bank of Poland (NBP) interventions drained between $80 and $100 million from the domestic forex market and clearly established the 2.55 percent from parity as the zloty's near-term resistance. 

 "Strong foreign entry in Monday's auction created a huge supply of dollars on the market, which was in turn drained by numerous NBP interventions," said Marek Szarlej of PBKS SA. 

 The zloty closed at 2.5472/82 to the dollar, down from yesterday's 2.5452/58, this loss reflecting the dollar's rise against the mark, and at 1.7253/55 to the mark, up from 1.7260/65. The central bank bought dollars at 2.5455, 2.5460 and 2.5480 zlotys and marks between 1.7255 and 1.7265 zlotys. 

 Dealers said the zloty's charge could ease on Wednesday, the settlement date for the T-bills, but that the sentiment was bound to return and keep the NBP defending resistance levels. 

 "Pressure is sure to be on the NBP, but judging by recent interventions, the bank intends to keep the zloty close to 2.5 percent from parity," said Andrzej Kopec of Bank Slaski SA. 

 The parity rate is the centre of the Polish currency's 14-percent trading band, set daily by the central bank using the value of a basket of currencies and a devaluation factor. 

 Dealers said T-bill yields continued to drop on the secondary market, with 52-week T-bills, sold on Monday with an average yield of 20.76 percent, trading today at 20.5 percent. 

 However, the amount of offers on the market increased from last week, which some dealers said could be a sign that yields were starting to bottom out.

title: Polish money rise slows on NBP draining - analysts.
text:
WARSAW, Oct 10 (Reuter) - Slower growth of Polish money supply in September despite fast growing hard currency reserves shows the central bank is successful in sterilising the market and points to non-monetary sources of inflation, analysts said. 

 Money supply grew 1.2 percent in September after a 3.3 percent rise in August while official reserves rose $1.245 billion to $12.99 billion in September after a $780 million growth in August. 

 Monthly inflation increased last month to about three percent from 0.4 percent in August and 0.9 percent in July. 

 "The high reserves growth in September and a slowdown in money supply at the same time shows the central bank copes very well with sterilising the market," said Maciej Krzak, chief economist at ING bank in Warsaw. 

 "This also undermines the argument of the finance ministry that inflation is mainly fuelled by money supply which slipped out of the central bank's control," he said. 

 The finance ministry has said inflation is mainly driven by the fast growth of official reserves and the resulting money supply increase. It has encouraged the central bank to both revalue the zloty and lower interest rates, saying this would block the inflow of short-term capital and cooled down exports. 

 The central bank is rejecting both measures at the moment, saying pressure from the reserves should be eliminated by opening up to imports and lowering the budget deficit. 

 Analysts said the treasury underestimated such elements as high inflation expectations, rises of government-controlled prices and the low competitiveness of the economy dominated by large, often monopolistic, state-owned firms. 

 The National Bank of Poland's officials said that apart from its money draining interventions, money supply was also lower because of seasonal factors. 

 "Although demand for money is higher in September, its turnover in the economy is also much faster, which helps bring down money supply," said Jacek Osinski, deputy head of the monetary policy department. 

 He said large foreign demand for Polish T-bills ahead of the September 18 official rate cut and unfulfilled expectations of a stronger zloty helped sterilise the market. 

 "Foreign purchases reduced the amount of T-bills available to Polish investors and their zloty surplus, together with zlotys created by the growing reserves, could be drained by the NBP instead of flowing out of the system," Osinski said. 

 Analysts also noted the 3.4 percent drop in credit for the budget sector which they said was a result of banks' switch to the attractive outright T-bill sales by the central bank. 

 They said the 1.2 percent fall of non-institutional currency deposits showed that Poles continued to switch from hard currency to the more attractive zloty deposits despite the two-point rate cut. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700

 Today's interventions surprised many dealers because they came at about 5.1 percent from the parity rate -- the centre of the 14-percent daily trading band -- below past intervention levels of more than 5.2 percent from parity.

title: NBP holds down zloty vs mark, lets it fall vs dlr.
text:

 They said the zloty's rise against the German currency, prompted by the dollar's sharp climb on world markets, would have been higher, were it not for the NBP action. 

 "Clearly there was mark-selling pressure, in line with the German unit's fall on world markets, but the NBP stopped the zloty's rise with an intervention," said Wojciech Czajkowski of Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA. 

 Dealers said however, the selling pressure remained strong despite the NBP move, depressing the mark/zloty rate back to the intervention level at 1.6670/90 after a brief rebound. 

 They said the today's NBP mark fixing at 1.6675 indicated the central bank received mostly mark sell offers from banks which wanted to square positions. 

 "The fixing below the market close indicates the NBP must have received mostly mark sell offers at lower levels signalling continuing currency selling pressure," said Marcin Szereda of Bank Handlowy SA.

title: Polish mkts to probe new NBP  intervention  levels.
text:
WARSAW, Aug 11 (Reuter) - The National Bank of Poland's relaxed approach to zloty rate swings this week is likely to keep the market guessing next week just how lenient the NBP's rate policy might have become, analysts said. 

 The NBP, usually stepping in with dollar and mark purchases when the zloty firmed to five percent from the daily parity rate, let the Polish currency rise to 5.1 percent against the mark on Thursday before it intervened to stop it. 

 The bank did not intervene buying dollars this week even though interbank offers often hovered at 5.08 percent from the dollar central parity. 

 "The NBP seemed to cut the zloty more slack this week, though it is not clear just how much more freedom it will get," said Marcin Szereda of Bank Handlowy SA. 

 Even the zloty's rise to 1.6920/30 against the mark today, or 5.13 percent from the parity rate, failed to prompt any central bank action. 

 Some analysts said however, the lack of interventions at the usual "five percent" level was just a central bank ruse to make the potential currency purchase levels less predictable. 

 "The NBP still wants to keep the zloty at the 'five percent' but is getting involved at slightly different levels to confuse the market and make the timing of the intervention less obvious," said Maciej Wegrzynski, treasurer at ING bank in Warsaw. 

 Analysts said daily currency revenues from exports, tourism and unregistered cross-border trade exerted strong upward pressure on the zloty, and were likely to keep it probing higher against the dollar and the mark next week. 

 But they also said the rise of the zloty was doomed to meet central bank resistance sooner rather than later because of an exports protection deal between the finance ministry and the central bank. 

 They said the ministry agreed to the partial flotation of the zloty in May, in exchange for a promise the NBP would not allow the Polish currency to firm more than five percent from the central parity rate. 

 The zloty strenghtened three percent after the flotation, but analysts said it would have gained more were it not for the NBP's firm stand.

title: Zloty closes weaker vs dollar despite small gains.
text:
WARSAW, Aug 8 (Reuter) - The Polish zloty failed to regain ground lost against the dollar overnight despite small intraday gains but was seen making another attempt at the upside tomorrow, dealers said. 

 They said today's clear dollar-selling trend combined with a lack of National Bank of Poland's dollar-buying interventions at the usual five percent from parity rate level could inspire banks to push the Polish currency higher tomorrow. 

 "The zloty's potential gains today were hampered by confusion as to how the NBP would react -- at which level it would step in with an intrevention" one dealer said. 

 The NBP usually started buying dollars or marks when the zloty firmed to five percent above the daily parity rate. 

 But today, for the third day in a row, the central bank not only allowed the zloty to trade lightly above the "five percent" level during the day, but also fixed the zloty at 5.04 percent above dollar parity and 5.02 percent above the mark parity. 

 "This signals a change in the NBP's forex market policy," said Piotr Konarski of Bank Handlowy SA. 

 "It is likely that the NBP will now defend the five percent level, but not from the central parity rate as until recently, but from the floating parity rate," he said. 

 The floating parity is based on the value of a basket of five currencies and follows rate movements on world markets. 

 On the interbank market the zloty closed at 2.3990/00 against the dollar, down from 2.3880/95 yesterday and 1.7015/25 against the mark, up from 1.7050/65. The NBP declined comment but some analysts hinted the bank was ready to become more flexible about the "five percent" level in order to keep the value of the basket of currencies unchanged. 

 On the money market one-day rates edged higher on a net outflow of 385 million zlotys in reverse repo payments and after the NBP's Open Market Committee (KKOOR) announced it had left its repo rate flat at 26.5 percent until August 21. 

 In the afternoon overnight and tomorrow/next rates rose 0.05 point to 26.6/26.65 and 26.6/26.7 percent respectively. 

 "It is likely that banks waited for the KKOOR announcement holding back with purchases in case the repo rate was cut and started searching for cash only after the announcement was published close to midday," one dealer said.

title: POLISH ZLOTY CONSOLIDATES VS DOLLAR.
text:

title: Huge  central bank interventions  ease Polish zloty.
text:
WARSAW, July 7 (Reuter) - The Polish zloty fell against the dollar in chaotic trade on Friday after the central bank bought an estimated $100 million on the domestic interbank market, dealers said. 

 "It was the biggest day of interventions far as I remember, there were big winners and big losers," said Marek Chrobak of Bank Zachodni SA. 

 Numerous central bank interventions triggered a wild dollar-buying trend and caused the zloty to ease by more than a grosz, or one hundreth, to the dollar from Thursday's close of 2.3605. 

 "Banks tried to close their positions, but the central bank had all of the dollars," one dealer said. 

 Continously large inflows of export revenues has put a strong upward pressure on the zloty and caused the National Bank of Poland (NBP), central bank, to intervene regularly on the interbank market since mid-May's float. 

 The zloty was partially floated on the domestic interbank market when its daily trading band widened from four to 14 percent on May 15. 

 The float, widely expected to strengthen the Polish unit and ease pressure of inflation-causing hard currency inflows, was followed by about a four percent appreciation of the zloty. 

 Since that time the NBP has consistantly bought small amounts of dollars and marks whenever market rates drifted much more than five percent from the parity rate, the centre of the daily trading band.

title: Polish zloty breaks NBP resistance vs mark.
text:
WARSAW, June 28 (Reuter) - The zloty firmed against the mark, breaking through the National Bank of Poland's (NBP) intervention levels, as the German unit lost a half a pfennig against the dollar on world markets, dealers said. 

 In speculative trade, the zloty strengthened to about 5.35 percent away from the central bank's parity rate, the mid-point of the daily 14-percent trading range, shattering old intervention levels of near 5.15 from parity. 

 "Many banks build long mark positions during the day in hopes of sell them, at a handsome profit, at the NBP's fixing," said one dealer. 

 Dealers said that today's mark fix, at 5.17 percent from parity and well below the market rate, was, in effect, another form of intervention buying of the German currency. 

 The zloty closed at 1.6881/93 to the mark, up from 1.6911/34 at opening, and yesterday's close of 1.6920/30. It closed at 2.3460/70 to the dollar, easing from 2.3420/30. 

 Dealers said the NBP's tactics were in a sharp contrast to yesterday, when the bank frequently intervened during the trading day, virtually freezing market rates and fixing currencies at closing market levels. 

 Most traders said today's approach gave the market more freedom to steer the exhchange but some said the frequent interventions were better because they offered stability. 

 Money market rates continued to be offered above the NBP's one day drainage rates of 26.5 percent, as some banks were making last minute efforts to beef up required monthly reserve levels, dealers said. 

 But the market's liquidity improved and tomorrow/next rates closed down 0.25 points at bid, flat at offer at 26.35/26.8, despite the central bank's 571 million zloty drainage.

title: Central bank interventions  freeze Polish zloty.
text:
WARSAW, June 27 (Reuter) - Poland's central bank intervened heavily on the domestic interbank market on Tuesday to stop the zloty's surge, casting doubts over the market's freedom to drive foreign exchange rates, bankers said. 

 The National Bank of Poland floated the zloty domestically last month by broadening the daily trading range from four to 14 percent around a central parity rate. The rate is set each day by the bank on the basis of pre-announced crawling devaluation and cross rates. 

 The central bank intervened at least three times on Tuesday as the zloty strengthened above the latest intervention level at 5.16 percent from parity. 

 After opening at 2.3425/55, five percent below parity, the zloty had no room to strengthen when the dollar started loosing ground to the mark internationally. 

 Dealers said because the parity rate is set once a day before the market opens, the central bank's stiff adherence to the five percent limit does not account for rate changes during the trading day. 

 "The parity rate becomes obsolete whenever the dollar makes significant moves internationally...and has little in common with the zloty's actual market value," one dealer said. 

 After the market was liberalised last month, bankers long on dollars due to booming exports, pushed the zloty about five percent above the parity rate, easing some pressure on money supply. 

 But then as they tried to push the zloty further, the central bank stepped in selling zlotys whenever the zloty/dollar rate fell more than five percent from parity. 

 "The 14-percent trading range is only theoretical. The practical range is between five and 5.2 percent below parity," said Marcin Stefaniuk, dealer at BDK bank. 

 "It's a one way market, the zloty hits a brick wall at the intervention level almost every day, and no matter what happens with the dollar and the mark (on world markets), the zloty simply cannot firm more," said Jacek Baprawski of PKO SA. 

Central bank officials have said that they are pleased with the current market level at five percent from parity because a further appreciation could harm exports. 

 They expect imports to pick up in the next few months, causing hard-currency outflows which would naturally depress the zloty and limit central bank intervention. 

 Some dealers said that if the central bank would free the zloty from the five percent band, the market would find its real balance only a half a point lower.

title: ZLOTY SEEN BRAVING  CENTRAL BANK INTERVENTION .
text:
WARSAW, June 12 (Reuter) - The Polish zloty is likely to test new highs against the dollar this week despite expected central bank dollar-buying interventions, buoyed by currency inflows from official and unregistered exports, analysts said. 

 The National Bank of Poland has been intervening on the market with dollar and mark purchases to slow down the Polish currency's climb after it was partially floated on the domestic interbank market on May 16. 

 The interventions have usually come when the Polish currency strengthened against the dollar or mark by more than five percent from the central parity rate -- the mid-point of a 14-percent trading band, calculated on the basis of a basket of five western currencies and a monthly devaluation factor. 

 Analysts said however that the intervention level at five percent below parity was untenable in view of the dollar's weakness on world markets and mounting dollar-selling pressure from exports revenues. 

 "The central bank might be forced to shift the 'five percent' level lower down (this) week because of the pile-up of currencies from exports and cross-border trade in banks," said Zbigniew Chmielewski, deputy treasurer at ING bank in Warsaw. 

 "It is likely to do so because its intention does not seem to be to reverse the zloty climb but only to slow it down, in which it succeded," he said. 

 The zloty ended the latest week at 2.3425/45 against the dollar, virtually flat compared with 2.3420/50 the Friday a week ago even though the dollar fell by almost one pfennig against the mark to about 1.40 during that period. 

 Analysts said the zloty's potential gains were capped by a rise in the central bank's parity rate to 2.3701 on Friday to the dollar today from 2.4614 a week earlier, which moved the five-percent below parity intervention level higher. 

 "The market wants to sell dollars but fear of a central bank intervention keeps the zloty down," said Artur Pilewicz of PKO BP bank. "There is almost no speculation because the risks are too high in case of an intervention, and banks deal mainly on clients' orders," he said. 

 On the money market dealers expected one-day zloty deposit rates to stay in the 25.5-26.5 percent range this week, pegged to the new one-day repo rate of 26.5 percent. 

 They said the central bank was likely to stage several open market drainages to help absorb the high liquidity of the market. Central bank figures show banks will receive a net inflow of some 2.62 billion zlotys next week. 

 "One-day rates are likely to stay in the 25.5-26.5 percent range with a bias towards the lower end because of the excess liquidity of the market," said Jaroslaw Maczkowski of BDK SA. 

 Dealers said that after several recent outright T-bill sales at which the NBP accepted higher yields than the finance ministry at its primary auction, the market was now likely to focus on today's 1.1 billion zloty primary T-bill tender. 

 They said banks are likely to bid for higher yields at today's auction expecting to place cash at an NBP outright if their bids are rejected. 

 "If the ministry plays it tough and keeps yields down, the NBP is likely to stage an outright sale to absorb the cash surplus not drained at the primary auction," said BDK's Maczkowski. 

 At the last outright sale the yield accepted by the NBP was about 0.3 point higher than that accepted by the treasury on a bill of comparable maturity at the primary auction. 

 -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 2 625 6303

title: Polish  central bank intervenes  to halt zloty rise.
text:
WARSAW, May 23 (Reuter) - The National Bank of Poland (NBP) intervened on the domestic foreign exchange market on Tuesday, halting the zloty's rapid appreciation against the dollar. 

 For the first time since it floated the currency on the domestic market last week, the central bank sold zlotys to banks at 2.3675 to the dollar after the Polish unit had soared by more than one percent in the morning. 

 The zloty briefly rose further to reach 2.3600, before the market became fully aware of the intervention and the currency slipped back. 

 "In our opinion, this appreciation was a little too fast and we wanted to give a signal to exporters, worried about the possibility of a major rise of the zloty," NBP's deputy president Krzysztof Barburski said. 

 The intervention gave domestic traders a taste of new hazards on the Polish foreign exchange market, brought by the flotation. 

 "We have what we wanted, a market run by supply and demand but one full of risks if you stick your neck out too far," said Marek Chrobak of Bank Zachodni SA. 

 Last Tuesday the NBP allowed banks to trade the zloty within a band of seven percent above and below a special parity rate. The rate is set each morning on the basis of world currency crosses and taking into account the monthly devaluation of the zloty against a basket of currencies. 

 Previously the zloty was confined to a four percent band and the central bank set the market tone each day by quoting currencies as the commercial banks did. The flotation gave the zloty, undervalued due to high foreign trade inflows, room for appreciation and allowed market forces greater influence on the exchange rate. 

 Bankers expected the currency to appreciate up to three percent after the move and the NBP intervention on Tuesday set the rate exactly at that level. 

 Economists have long advocated a zloty revaluation, either by floating the currency or through an administrative one-off appreciation, saying this was the only way to ease monetary pressure caused by swelling hard currency reserves. The central bank chose the former, believing it would guarantee a gradual appreciation that would be less harmful to Poland's booming exports. 

 Following the float, the zloty was appreciating slowly but this week the trend accelerated and Tuesday's zloty gains moved it five percent away from the central bank's parity rate of 2.4830, prompting the intervention. 

 "Our role is to stabilise the trend and not to allow large volatility," central banker Barburski said. "In my opinion the market was speculative today." 

 Following the NBP action rates stabilised at around 2.3670 to the dollar and bankers said the intervention level had become a resistance point for the zloty.

title: Poland 's NBP  interventions  to serve monetary goals.
text:
WARSAW, May 14 (Reuter) - Poland's central bank will be guided by long-term monetary goals and the state of its foreign currency reserves while intervening on the domestic market after a partial float of the zloty, the bank's deputy head said on Saturday. 

 Krzysztof Barburski told a meeting of bankers that floating of the zloty on the domestic market on May 16 would shift the main role in setting the exchange rate from the National Bank of Poland to commercial banks. 

 "The shaping of the rates will principally depend on you," he said at an annual conference of Polish foreign exchange dealers. 

 "Our main guidance will be long-term monetary policy targets and the second important factor will be the state of reserves." 

 Under the new rules, domestic banks will be free to set exchange rates within a 14 percent band around the central bank's mid-rate. 

 The rate will be set each morning on the basis of world market rates and will also take into account the preannounced monthly devaluation of the zloty, now at 1.2 percent. 

 Up to now the band was only four percent and the banks were able to deal with the central bank only at this band's top and bottom limits. This gave the central bank the dominant role in setting the exchange rates. 

 Now, Barburski said, the central bank will only intervene on the market to send rates in a desired direction. 

 It will also hold an early afternoon auction, during which it will make a fixing, based on the bids and offers from banks willing to square positions with the central bank. 

 Barburski said this method would allow fixing to reflect more closely market rates. 

 "The fixing should be close to the average between the interbank market's bid and offer rates," he said. 

 The fixing, announced at about 1500 local time, would serve as a reference for all transactions with non-banking clients. 

 Barburski said the central bank would intervene in such a way as to make its policy predictable by market players. 

 "You will be making decisions about rates but we want you to be able to understand our policy," he said. 

 He said the market could be very volatile initially but should gradually settle down once the new rules are digested. 

 He also said the interventions would aim at guiding the market rather than pushing the rates in a desired way. 

 Analysts say the central bank has decided on a partial float of the zloty in the hope that it would allow the domestic currency to appreciate, stemming the rapid growth of foreign exchange reserves. 

 They also say the move would make monetary policy more flexible and the exchange rate more in tune with market condidions. 

 Bankers estimate that the zloty, which closed on Friday at 2.46 to the dollar, could appreciate by up to three percent after the float, but they also say the size of the appreciation will be chiefly determined by the central bank. 

 One banker said that shortly after the flotation, the central bank was likely to impose, through interventions, the desired level of appreciation, only later leaving it to the market to set the rate. 

 "I think the bank will make a policy decision about the scope of the zloty appreciation because this is why these new regulations were introduced in the first place," the banker said. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 2 625 6303
